# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any - `docsrs`
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Deserialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Serialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.

# time - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/time/0.3.49/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/time/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

This crate exposes a number of features. These can be enabled or disabled as shown
[in Cargo’s documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/features.html). Features
are *disabled* by default unless otherwise noted.

Reliance on a given feature is always indicated alongside the item definition.

-
`std`(*enabled by default, implicitly enables*)`alloc`This enables a number of features that depend on the standard library.
-
`alloc`(*enabled by default via*)`std`Enables a number of features that require the ability to dynamically allocate memory.
-
`macros`Enables macros that provide compile-time verification of values and intuitive syntax.
-
`formatting`(*implicitly enables*)`std`Enables formatting of most structs.
-
`parsing`Enables parsing of most structs.
-
`local-offset`(*implicitly enables*)`std`This feature enables a number of methods that allow obtaining the system’s UTC offset.
-
`large-dates`By default, only years within the ±9999 range (inclusive) are supported. If you need support for years outside this range, consider enabling this feature; the supported range will be increased to ±999,999. Note that enabling this feature has some costs, as it means forgoing some optimizations. Ambiguities may be introduced when parsing that would not otherwise exist.
-
`serde`Enables `serde`
-
`serde-human-readable`(*implicitly enables*)`serde`,`formatting`, and`parsing`Allows `serde`representations to use a human-readable format. This is determined by the serializer, not the user. If this feature is not enabled or if the serializer requests a non-human-readable format, a format optimized for binary representation will be used.Libraries should never enable this feature, as the decision of what format to use should be up to the user.
-
`rand`(*implicitly enables*)`rand08`,`rand09`, and`rand010`Previously, this would enable support for `rand`0.8. Since the release of`rand`0.9, the feature has been split into`rand08`and`rand09`to allow support for both versions.`rand`0.10 has since been added. For backwards compatibility and simplicity, this feature enables support for*all*series.It is strongly recommended to enable the version you need directly, as enabling `rand`will needlessly pull in all versions.
-
`rand08`,`rand09`,`rand010`Enables `rand`0.8`rand`0.9`rand`0.10
-
`quickcheck`(*implicitly enables*)`alloc`Enables [quickcheck](https://docs.rs/quickcheck)support for all types.
-
`wasm-bindgen`Enables `wasm-bindgen`[JavaScript dates](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-bindgen/api/js_sys/struct.Date.html), as well as obtaining the UTC offset from JavaScript.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::error::`- [Error](https://docs.rs/error/enum.Error.html);

- Macros to construct statically known values.

- Parsing for various types.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Date](https://docs.rs/struct.Date.html)
- Date in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.
- [Duration](https://docs.rs/struct.Duration.html)
- A span of time with nanosecond precision.
- [Offset](https://docs.rs/struct.OffsetDateTime.html)- Date - Time

# license - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/LICENSE

## Expand description

**Embedded license information from  SPDX.**

Use the licenses directly.

```
use license::License;
use license::licenses::Bsd3Clause;
let bsd3 = Bsd3Clause;
assert!(bsd3.is_osi_approved());
assert_eq!(bsd3.name(), r#"BSD 3-Clause "New" or "Revised" License"#);
```
Get the license by parsing the license id.

```
use license::License;
let apache2: &dyn License = "Apache-2.0".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(apache2.name(), "Apache License 2.0");
```
License exceptions are also supported.

```
use license::Exception;
let gcc: &dyn Exception = "GCC-exception-3.1".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(gcc.name(), "GCC Runtime Library exception 3.1");
```
[Serde](https://crates.io/crates/serde) is supported with the `serde` feature.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [exceptions](https://docs.rs/exceptions/index.html)
- All supported exceptions.
- [licenses](https://docs.rs/licenses/index.html)
- All supported licenses.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)- Error
- Error returned when parsing license and exception ids.

# causal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/causal/0.19.0/causal/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#causal)Causal

Event-sourcing runtime for Rust, [KurrentDB](https://www.kurrent.io/)-aligned:
a typed `Event → Reactor → Event` loop over an append-only event log.
Runs entirely in-memory for tests ([ MemoryStore](https://docs.rs/memory_store/struct.MemoryStore.html)); production backends
(KurrentDB event log, Postgres cursors/snapshots) live in

`causal_replay`.The vocabulary mirrors KurrentDB’s where the concepts overlap:
[ EventData](https://docs.rs/types/struct.EventData.html) /

[,](https://docs.rs/types/struct.RecordedEvent.html)

`RecordedEvent``causation_id` /
`workflow_id`, [(0-indexed),](https://docs.rs/types/struct.StreamRevision.html)

`StreamRevision`[for optimistic concurrency,](https://docs.rs/types/enum.StreamState.html)

`StreamState``{category}-{subject_id}` stream names.[§](https://docs.rs#guarantees)Guarantees

- **At-least-once delivery, idempotent appends**— reactor outputs carry deterministic- `event_id`s, so crash-redelivery dedups on append.
- **Replay determinism**— no wall-clock inside consumer bodies; aggregate state is a pure fold of the log.
- **Quiescence**—- `emit(...).settled()`resolves when the event’s workflow chain has been observed by every consumer.
- **OCC where you opt in**— the- `Engine::append`decider path enforces- `StreamState`

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use causal::{Ctx, EngineBuilder, Event, Events, Reactor};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use uuid::Uuid;
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct OrderPlaced { order_id: Uuid, total: f64 }
impl Event for OrderPlaced {
    const NAME: &'static str = "order_placed";
    fn subject_id(&self) -> Uuid { self.order_id }
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct ShipmentRequested { order_id: Uuid }
impl Event for ShipmentRequested {
    const NAME: &'static str = "shipment_requested";
    fn subject_id(&self) -> Uuid { self.order_id }
}
struct ShipOnPlaced;
#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl Reactor for ShipOnPlaced {
    type Trigger = OrderPlaced;
    const NAME: &'static str = "ship_on_placed";
    async fn react(&self, t: &OrderPlaced, _ctx: Ctx<'_>) -> anyhow::Result<Events> {
        Ok(causal::events![ShipmentRequested { order_id: t.order_id }])
    }
}
let engine = EngineBuilder::memory()
    .with_reactor(ShipOnPlaced)
    .build()
    .await?;
// Persists the event, stamps causation/workflow, and resolves once
// ShipOnPlaced has reacted and its output has landed in the log.
engine.emit(OrderPlaced { order_id: Uuid::new_v4(), total: 99.99 })
    .settled()
    .await?;
```
The `#[event]` macro (feature `macros`, on by default) generates the
[ Event](https://docs.rs/event/trait.Event.html) impl from a struct declaration
(

`#[event(name = "order_placed", subject_id = "order_id")]`); the
example hand-rolls it to show the full trait surface.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [aggregate](https://docs.rs/aggregate/index.html)
- `Aggregate`marker +- `Apply<F: Event>`extension.
- [aggregator](https://docs.rs/aggregator/index.html)
- Aggregator registry — manages aggregate definitions and state.
- [checkpoint_](https://docs.rs/checkpoint_store/index.html)- store
- Per-consumer cursor storage + reactor retry-tracking traits.
- [clock](https://docs.rs/clock/index.html)
- Calendar-clock injection — one half of Primitive 6’s two-clock rule.
- [consumer_](https://docs.rs/consumer_lease/index.html)- lease
- Exclusive consumer lease — prevents two servers from processing the same consumer’s triggers simultaneously.
- [contexts](https://docs.rs/contexts/index.html)
- Single `Ctx`type passed to all consumer bodies. Three separate context types would add no safety beyond what the runtime already enforces.
- [decision_](https://docs.rs/decision_store/index.html)- store
- `DecisionStore`— one durable decision per- `(consumer, trigger)`.
- [effect_](https://docs.rs/effect_store/index.html)- store
- `EffectStore`— make side-effecting reactors safe under at-least-once delivery.
- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- `Engine`+- `EngineBuilder`— the public runtime surface.
- [event](https://docs.rs/event/index.html)
- `Event`trait — application-facing surface for events.
- [event_](https://docs.rs/event_id_registry/index.html)- id_ - registry
- `EventIdRegistry`— an authoritative, unbounded global index of appended- `event_id`s, so- `Any`(idempotent) appends can recognize a redelivery no matter how deep the original output is buried.
- [event_](https://docs.rs/event_log/index.html)- log
- Append-only event log trait — the write side of the durable event store.
- [event_](https://docs.rs/event_type/index.html)- type
- Single owner of event-kind validation and matching.
- [failure](https://docs.rs/failure/index.html)
- The retry taxonomy (BLOCKING-2) — error classes, declared by the reactor, that decide retry policy. No blanket policy in either direction: blanket bounded-retry turns a ten-minute infra outage into a mass manual-replay incident; blanket infinite-retry turns a poison payload into a permanently wedged partition.
- [memory_](https://docs.rs/memory_store/index.html)- store
- In-memory backend: `EventLogBackend`+`CheckpointStore`+`ReactorCheckpoint`+`SnapshotStore`(+`ReactorObserver`and the inspector read surface).
- [multi_](https://docs.rs/multi_projector/index.html)- projector
- `MultiProjector`— declared-subscription cross-domain event consumer.
- [projection](https://docs.rs/projection/index.html)
- Projection / consumer start-position configuration.
- [projection_](https://docs.rs/projection_failure/index.html)- failure
- Poison-park failure handling shared by the serial projection runners
(`ProjectionRunner``MultiProjectorRunner`
- [projection_](https://docs.rs/projection_runner/index.html)- runner
- Runner that drives `Projector``EventLogBackend::read_all`.
- [projector](https://docs.rs/projector/index.html)
- `Projector`trait — idempotent at-least-once external state.
- [reactor](https://docs.rs/reactor/index.html)
- `Reactor`trait — pure decisions producing new facts.
- [reactor_](https://docs.rs/reactor_observer/index.html)- observer
- `ReactorObserver`— telemetry hook for reactor execution and aggregate folds. The engine calls these methods at well-defined points so observability sinks (the in-memory inspector backend, external tracing, etc.) can capture causal-chain history without the engine itself having to know about durability of trace data.
- [reactor_](https://docs.rs/reactor_runner/index.html)- runner
- Partitioned runner for `Reactor`
- [snapshot_](https://docs.rs/snapshot_store/index.html)- store
- Snapshot persistence trait — separate from the event log so the snapshot backend can be swapped independently (Postgres log + S3 snapshots, Kurrent log + Postgres snapshots, etc.). Backends implement this trait directly.
- [types](https://docs.rs/types/index.html)
- Core data types for the causal event log.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [events](https://docs.rs/macro.events.html)
- Universal return macro for `Reactor::react``Events`

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [aggregators](https://docs.rs/attr.aggregators.html)
- Collects `#[aggregator]`functions in a module into a`fn aggregators() -> Vec<Aggregator>`.
- [async_](https://docs.rs/attr.async_trait.html)- trait
- [event](https://docs.rs/attr.event.html)
- Marks a struct as a causal fact, generating its `causal::Event`impl.
- [projectors](https://docs.rs/attr.projectors.html)
- Turns a module of plain async functions into registered
[`Projector`]s / [`MultiProjector`]s — same contract as`reactors`
- [reactors](https://docs.rs/attr.reactors.html)
- Turns a module of plain async functions into registered [`Reactor`]s — the fn body is the Primitive-2 body, untouched; the macro removes trait ceremony only.

# causal_inspector_utils - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/causal_inspector_utils/0.19.0/causal_inspector_utils/

## Expand description

Describe DSL for the causal inspector UI.

Provides [ Block](https://docs.rs/enum.Block.html) — a set of visual primitives that handlers return to
describe their current state. Blocks are serialized to JSON in the store
and rendered inline on reactor nodes in the causal flow diagram.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use causal_inspector_utils::{Block, ChecklistItem, State};
let blocks = vec![
    Block::progress("Scrape phases", 0.75),
    Block::checklist("Steps", vec![
        ChecklistItem::new("Fetch data", true),
        ChecklistItem::new("Transform", false),
    ]),
    Block::status("Pipeline", State::Running),
];
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Checklist](https://docs.rs/struct.ChecklistItem.html)- Item
- A checklist item with text and done state.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/enum.Block.html)
- A visual primitive rendered inline on reactor nodes in the causal flow diagram.
- [State](https://docs.rs/enum.State.html)
- Named state for a `Block::Status`

# hrdr_app - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hrdr-app/0.2.1/hrdr_app/

## Expand description

`hrdr-app` — the UI-agnostic application core shared by hrdr’s frontends.

Logic that is identical regardless of how it’s rendered lives here so the TUI
(`hrdr-tui`) and GUI (`hrdr-gui`) share one implementation instead of each
reimplementing it. Today: the slash-command registry, alias resolution, and
“quit command” detection. More (help metadata is already here) will move in
as the frontends converge.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [expand_](https://docs.rs/expand_msg/index.html)- msg
- `/expand`status lines (both frontends show the same wording).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Chat](https://docs.rs/struct.ChatPalette.html)- Palette
- hrdr’s chat-role colors as resolved from an hjkl theme (before frontend fallbacks).
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigWatcherGuard.html)- Watcher - Guard
- Keeps a config watch alive; drop it to stop watching.
- [CtxGauge](https://docs.rs/struct.CtxGauge.html)
- The context gauge’s raw data, for frontends that can draw a real progress bar (the GUI) instead of the character-cell fill the text runs encode.
- [Find](https://docs.rs/struct.FindState.html)- State
- The `/find`/`/next`/`/prev`state machine: active query + last-visited message number. Both frontends hold one (the GUI behind signals) and route the returned`FindAction`
- [Highlight](https://docs.rs/struct.HighlightCache.html)- Cache
- Incremental code-block highlighter with a small LRU of in-progress blocks.
- [History](https://docs.rs/struct.HistoryBrowser.html)- Browser
- Input-history browsing shared by the frontends: record with
consecutive-duplicate skip + `MAX_HISTORY`
- [Resume](https://docs.rs/struct.ResumePlan.html)- Plan
- What restoring a session changes beyond the host’s own state swap: the working directory to adopt (if any) and the system lines to show, in order.
- [Role](https://docs.rs/struct.RoleStyle.html)- Style
- Renderer-agnostic style spec: which theme slots to paint with. `fg: None`means inverted text (black) over`bg`— used by the context-gauge fill.
- [Save](https://docs.rs/struct.SaveOutcome.html)- Outcome
- The result of an auto-save: the session’s file id, and whether this call was the one that first assigned it (so the frontend can notify once).
- [Status](https://docs.rs/struct.StatusInputs.html)- Inputs
- Everything the status bar shows, gathered by the frontend.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/struct.StatusRun.html)- Run
- One styled run of text within a status section.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/struct.StatusSeg.html)- Seg
- One status-bar section: a drop `priority`(higher = dropped first when the TUI truncates) and its styled runs.`gauge`carries the context gauge’s raw data when this section is it — text frontends use the pre-split fill/rest runs, pixel frontends draw a real bar from the gauge.
- [UiConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.UiConfig.html)
- Frontend/display configuration. Loaded from the same
`~/.config/hrdr/config.toml`+`HRDR_*`env vars as`hrdr_agent::AgentConfig`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [CtxLevel](https://docs.rs/enum.CtxLevel.html)
- How full the context window is, for the gauge’s fill color.
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/enum.DiffLineKind.html)- Line - Kind
- Semantic role of one unified-diff line, for `/diff`coloring — the classification both frontends map onto their theme.
- [Entry](https://docs.rs/enum.Entry.html)
- One rendered item in the transcript.
- [Expand](https://docs.rs/enum.ExpandMode.html)- Mode
- What `/expand`should do to tool output (parsed by the shared dispatcher; applied by the frontend, which owns the expansion state).
- [Find](https://docs.rs/enum.FindAction.html)- Action
- What a `/find`,`/next`,`/prev`, or`/goto`resolved to. The frontends only differ in how they scroll — the parsing, cycling, wrap-around, and status lines are all here.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/enum.LineKind.html)- Kind
- How an async result line should be displayed.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/enum.StatusBarMode.html)- BarMode
- How the status bar behaves when it doesn’t fit the terminal width.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/enum.StatusRole.html)- Role
- Semantic color role of a status run — frontends map these to theme colors.
- [Theme](https://docs.rs/enum.ThemeSlot.html)- Slot
- Theme slot a semantic role colors from. Both frontends’ themes expose these eight colors (under their own field names); mapping slot → concrete color is the only per-frontend piece.
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/enum.TimestampStyle.html)- Style
- Per-message timestamp display style.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [BELL_](https://docs.rs/constant.BELL_MIN_SECS.html)- MIN_ - SECS
- Minimum turn duration before the finish nudge fires (terminal bell in the TUI, desktop notification in the GUI) — quick replies stay silent.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_TODO_TTL.html)- TODO_ - TTL
- Default lifetime (in turns) a completed TODO item stays visible before it’s pruned: the turn it finishes plus four more.
- [HELP_](https://docs.rs/constant.HELP_GROUPS.html)- GROUPS
- Commands grouped by theme, for a readable help listing.
- [INIT_](https://docs.rs/constant.INIT_PROMPT.html)- PROMPT
- Instruction sent to the model by `/init`to author an`AGENTS.md`.
- [INPUT_](https://docs.rs/constant.INPUT_MAX_ROWS.html)- MAX_ - ROWS
- Max text rows the input box auto-grows to (both frontends).
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_HISTORY.html)- HISTORY
- Max input-history entries kept (in memory and on disk).
- [PROJECT_](https://docs.rs/constant.PROJECT_DOCS_LOADED_MSG.html)- DOCS_ - LOADED_ - MSG
- Startup notice when `AGENTS.md`was gathered into the system prompt.
- [RELOAD_](https://docs.rs/constant.RELOAD_HOT_MSG.html)- HOT_ - MSG
- [RELOAD_](https://docs.rs/constant.RELOAD_MANUAL_MSG.html)- MANUAL_ - MSG
- `/reload`+ hot-reload status lines (both frontends).
- [RESUME_](https://docs.rs/constant.RESUME_BUSY_MSG.html)- BUSY_ - MSG
- Guard shown when `/resume`is attempted mid-turn (the running turn holds the agent mutex: the message swap would silently no-op while the transcript and session id switched, and the turn’s autosave would then overwrite the resumed session’s file with the old conversation).
- [SLASH_](https://docs.rs/constant.SLASH_COMMANDS.html)- COMMANDS
- The slash commands, as `(name, one-line description)`. Frontends render this however they like (a completion popup, a`/`menu, a help screen).
- [TOOL_](https://docs.rs/constant.TOOL_ARGS_PREVIEW.html)- ARGS_ - PREVIEW
- Character width of the one-line tool-args preview (both frontends).
- [TUI_](https://docs.rs/constant.TUI_ONLY_COMMANDS.html)- ONLY_ - COMMANDS
- Commands only the TUI implements today (terminal-coupled, or not yet ported
to the GUI). Canonical names; aliases resolve before matching. The GUI
filters these out of completion and `/help`, and answers with a notice instead of sending the text to the model.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Command](https://docs.rs/trait.CommandHost.html)- Host
- The capabilities a frontend exposes so the shared commands can drive it.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [active_](https://docs.rs/fn.active_file_token.html)- file_ - token
- If an `@…`file mention is being typed at the end of`input`, return the byte offset of the`@`and the partial query after it. Requires the`@`to start a token (preceded by start-of-input or whitespace) with no whitespace after it.
- [age_](https://docs.rs/fn.age_completed_todos.html)- completed_ - todos
- Age out finished TODO items in place. Stamps each completed item with the
`turn`it was first seen finished (in`stamps`, keyed by content), then drops any completed item that has been finished for`ttl`turns. Stamps for items no longer present as completed are forgotten, so a re-completed item ages from scratch. Pending / in-progress items are kept.
- [agent_](https://docs.rs/fn.agent_cwd.html)- cwd
- The tools’ working directory: the agent’s cwd when the lock is free (a turn may hold it), else the process cwd.
- [cancel_](https://docs.rs/fn.cancel_message.html)- message
- The cancel notice both frontends show (with the discarded-queue count).
- [classify_](https://docs.rs/fn.classify_diff_line.html)- diff_ - line
- Classify one line of a unified diff (see `DiffLineKind`
- [clipboard_](https://docs.rs/fn.clipboard_copy_status.html)- copy_ - status
- Copy `text`to the OS clipboard, returning the status line both frontends show.`cb`is the frontend’s long-lived clipboard handle (`None`when the platform has none).
- [clipboard_](https://docs.rs/fn.clipboard_read_text.html)- read_ - text
- Read the OS clipboard as text (`/paste`).
- [compaction_](https://docs.rs/fn.compaction_message.html)- message
- The system line a finished compaction shows — identical in both frontends.
- [config_](https://docs.rs/fn.config_mtime.html)- mtime
- Modified-time of the user config file, for hot-reload dedup guards.
- [conversation_](https://docs.rs/fn.conversation_to_json.html)- to_ - json
- The conversation’s user/assistant turns as a JSON array of `{n, role, content}`.
- [conversation_](https://docs.rs/fn.conversation_to_markdown.html)- to_ - markdown
- The conversation’s user/assistant turns as Markdown.
- [ctx_](https://docs.rs/fn.ctx_level_slot.html)- level_ - slot
- The gauge-fill color slot for a context-usage level (also used by the GUI’s real progress-bar gauge).
- [diff_](https://docs.rs/fn.diff_kind_slot.html)- kind_ - slot
- Diff-line coloring semantics (additions green, deletions red, hunk headers
in the user accent, file headers/context dim) — shared with
`crate::classify_diff_line`
- [dispatch](https://docs.rs/fn.dispatch.html)
- Handle a `/…`command shared by both frontends. Returns`true`if it was a recognized command (and thus shouldn’t be sent to the model). Unknown input returns`false`so the caller can pass it to the model or handle it locally.
- [display_](https://docs.rs/fn.display_dir.html)- dir
- Display form of `cwd`, with the home directory collapsed to`~`.
- [endpoint_](https://docs.rs/fn.endpoint_health_warning.html)- health_ - warning
- Probe the endpoint (list its models) and return a warning line when it
looks unreachable or doesn’t advertise `model`;`None`when healthy. The startup health-check core — both frontends spawn it and surface the warning as a system line before the first turn.
- [expand_](https://docs.rs/fn.expand_mentions.html)- mentions
- Expand `@file`mentions in`input`by appending the referenced files’ contents (resolved under`cwd`), for sending to the model. Each distinct readable`@path`is attached once under a trailing “Referenced files” section, truncated at 100 KiB on a char boundary; unreadable/missing/ duplicate references are skipped. Returns`input`unchanged when nothing resolves. The display copy should keep the bare`@path`; only the sent copy carries the expansion.
- [export_](https://docs.rs/fn.export_conversation.html)- conversation
- Write the conversation to a file per a `/export [--json] [file]`argument, returning the path written and its line count. With no file, a timestamped`hrdr-transcript-<date>.{md,json}`in`cwd`is used.
- [find_](https://docs.rs/fn.find_hits.html)- hits
- 1-based message numbers whose user/assistant text contains `query`(case-insensitive substring). Message numbers count only user/assistant entries, matching the numbering the frontends display.
- [first_](https://docs.rs/fn.first_message_since.html)- message_ - since
- The number of the first user/assistant message stamped at/after `cutoff`.`times`is parallel to`entries`(index i is entry i’s local timestamp).
- [fmt_](https://docs.rs/fn.fmt_count.html)- count
- Compact token count: `840`,`12.4k`,`1.8M`.
- [git_](https://docs.rs/fn.git_branch.html)- branch
- Current git branch (or short detached-HEAD sha) by walking up from `cwd`to the repo root and reading`.git/HEAD`. Cheap, no subprocess.
- [git_](https://docs.rs/fn.git_working_diff.html)- working_ - diff
- The working-tree `git diff`for`cwd`(stdout on success, stderr message on failure). Shared by`/diff`.
- [goto_](https://docs.rs/fn.goto_action.html)- action
- `/goto <N | 5m | 1h | top | end>`— resolve- `arg`against a transcript with- `count`displayed messages.- `first_since(cutoff)`returns the number of the first message at/after that instant (the frontend’s timestamp lookup).
- [help_](https://docs.rs/fn.help_body.html)- body
- The grouped, aligned `/help`body: a`Commands`header followed by each`HELP_GROUPS`section with its commands and descriptions. Frontends append their own keybinding “Tips:” tail (those keys differ per frontend).
- [help_](https://docs.rs/fn.help_body_for.html)- body_ - for
- Like `help_body``show`accepts — so a frontend’s`/help`advertises exactly what it supports (the GUI passes its`CommandHost::supports_command`
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_known_command.html)- known_ - command
- Whether `cmd`(with or without the leading`/`; aliases welcome) is a registered slash command at all — used by frontends to tell “command I don’t support” apart from “not a command, send it to the model”.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_quit_command.html)- quit_ - command
- Whether a submitted line is a common “quit the session” command, matched
across popular CLIs/REPLs/editors so users feel at home: bare `exit`/`quit`, the`/exit``/quit``/bye`slash family, and vim’s`:q`family.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_tui_only.html)- tui_ - only
- Whether `cmd`(with or without the leading`/`; aliases welcome) is a TUI-only command per`TUI_ONLY_COMMANDS`
- [last_](https://docs.rs/fn.last_fenced_block.html)- fenced_ - block
- The last fenced (`…`) code block in markdown`md`, without the fences.
- [latest_](https://docs.rs/fn.latest_session_for_cwd.html)- session_ - for_ - cwd
- The most recent saved session for `cwd`that has actual conversation content (more than just the system prompt) — the startup auto-resume lookup shared by both frontends.`None`= nothing to resume, start fresh.
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_history.html)- history
- Load persisted single-line input history (most recent `MAX_HISTORY`
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_hjkl_theme.html)- hjkl_ - theme
- Load an hjkl theme TOML from `path`, falling back to hjkl’s bundled default when`path`is`None`or fails to parse (both frontends’ load policy).
- [message_](https://docs.rs/fn.message_count.html)- count
- Number of user/assistant messages in the transcript.
- [messages_](https://docs.rs/fn.messages_to_entries.html)- to_ - entries
- Rebuild display entries from a restored message history (`/resume`, startup auto-resume) — shared so the TUI and GUI reconstruct identically. User and non-empty assistant texts become entries; each assistant`tool_calls`entry is paired with its`role:"tool"`result by call id (the`Error:`prefix convention marks a failed call). Other roles are skipped. Frontends map the returned entries into their own representation (the TUI stores them as-is, the GUI wraps each in its reactive signals).
- [nth_](https://docs.rs/fn.nth_message_text.html)- message_ - text
- The text of the Nth (1-based) user/assistant message, if any.
- [open_](https://docs.rs/fn.open_system_handler.html)- system_ - handler
- Launch the OS default handler for `path`(`xdg-open`on Linux/BSD,`open`on macOS,`start`on Windows), detached — the child outlives the call.
- [panel_](https://docs.rs/fn.panel_bg_rgb.html)- bg_ - rgb
- Panel background RGB for code blocks and tool output: the syntect theme’s background with a dark fallback. Frontends convert to their color type.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_duration.html)- duration
- Parse a relative duration like `30s`,`5m`,`1h`,`2d`into seconds.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_msg_range.html)- msg_ - range
- Parse a message spec: `N`→`(N, N)`, or`N-M`→`(N, M)`(1-based, inclusive). Returns`None`for invalid or zero/reversed ranges.
- [persist_](https://docs.rs/fn.persist_history.html)- history
- Persist input history (one entry per line; multi-line entries are skipped to keep the line-based file well-formed). Best-effort — filesystem errors are silently ignored.
- [rank_](https://docs.rs/fn.rank_file_matches.html)- file_ - matches
- Rank file paths against an `@file``query`and return the best (up to 8). Empty query keeps input order (shortest paths first); otherwise basename prefix-matches rank above anywhere-substring matches, ties broken by shorter path then lexicographically. Case-insensitive.
- [relative_](https://docs.rs/fn.relative_time.html)- time
- Human-friendly elapsed time since `then`, with compound units for the larger ranges (`now`,`42s ago`,`5m ago`,`1h30m ago`,`2d3h ago`).
- [reload_](https://docs.rs/fn.reload_invalid_message.html)- invalid_ - message
- Invalid config file on reload: keep the current settings and warn.
- [reload_](https://docs.rs/fn.reload_project_docs.html)- project_ - docs
- Re-read `AGENTS.md`into the system prompt (used by`/reload`and after an`/init`turn writes the file). Returns the standard system line when project docs were loaded,`None`when there are none.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_alias.html)- alias
- Resolve a slash-command alias to its canonical name (case-insensitive), so users coming from other agents can use familiar names. Unknown names pass through unchanged.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_under.html)- under
- Resolve `path`against`base`: absolute paths pass through unchanged, relative ones are joined onto`base`.
- [resume_](https://docs.rs/fn.resume_plan.html)- plan
- The shared `/resume`semantics both frontends apply: follow the session’s working directory (in-process only) and surface the same notices.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_compaction.html)- compaction
- The shared compaction core (`/compact`and threshold auto-compaction): lock the agent and summarize.`Ok((before, after))`with`before == after`means there was nothing to compact.
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_agent_session.html)- agent_ - session
- Async wrapper over `save_session``CommandHost::autosave`); the TUI’s synchronous`try_lock`autosave keeps its own snapshot but funnels into the same`save_session`
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_session.html)- session
- Persist a conversation as a session (best-effort; filesystem errors are
swallowed). Returns `None`when there’s nothing worth saving yet (no user message). Otherwise it builds and writes the session under`cwd`, assigning a stable file id from the name when`existing_id`is`None`(via`hrdr_agent::unique_session_id``label`overrides the auto-derived name (the first user line); pass`None`to use the derived one.
- [session_](https://docs.rs/fn.session_list_text.html)- list_ - text
- The `/sessions`listing as a display string. With`all`, every directory’s sessions are shown (each row tagged with its cwd); otherwise only those whose cwd matches`cwd`. Returns a friendly empty-state message when there are none.
- [session_](https://docs.rs/fn.session_name_from.html)- name_ - from
- A short session name derived from the first user message (first line, trimmed,
capped at 60 chars). Falls back to `"untitled"`when there’s no usable text.
- [session_](https://docs.rs/fn.session_saved_notice.html)- saved_ - notice
- The one-time notice when a session file is first created.
- [sessions_](https://docs.rs/fn.sessions_all_flag.html)- all_ - flag
- Whether a `/sessions`argument requests every directory’s sessions.
- [should_](https://docs.rs/fn.should_auto_compact.html)- auto_ - compact
- Whether the context usage warrants a proactive compaction before more work
— the `auto_compact`threshold check, shared by both frontends.`last_prompt_tokens`is the latest model call’s prompt size.
- [should_](https://docs.rs/fn.should_bell.html)- bell
- Whether a finished turn warrants the nudge: the knob is on and the turn ran
at least `BELL_MIN_SECS`
- [slash_](https://docs.rs/fn.slash_completions.html)- completions
- Commands matching the in-progress `/…`input (empty once a space is typed).
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_file_index.html)- file_ - index
- Build the `@file`completion index off the UI thread —`walk_files``on_done`receives the file list there (send it back through your UI channel).
- [startup_](https://docs.rs/fn.startup_config_warning.html)- config_ - warning
- Startup warning when the config file exists but is invalid (the running config already fell back to defaults + env).
- [status_](https://docs.rs/fn.status_role_style.html)- role_ - style
- The one place the status-bar color semantics live — frontends resolve the returned slots against their theme instead of re-deciding role → color.
- [status_](https://docs.rs/fn.status_sections.html)- sections
- Build the status sections in display order. Priorities (drop order under truncation, highest first): ttft 6, effort 5, tokens 4, branch 3, model 2, context 1, dir 0.
- [syntax_](https://docs.rs/fn.syntax_set.html)- set
- The bundled syntax set, deserialized once.
- [syntect_](https://docs.rs/fn.syntect_theme.html)- theme
- The highlight theme (base16-ocean.dark, falling back to any bundled theme).
- [transcript_](https://docs.rs/fn.transcript_to_json.html)- to_ - json
- The conversation as a pretty-printed JSON array of `{n, role, time, content}`objects (user/assistant messages only).`times`is parallel to`entries`.
- [transcript_](https://docs.rs/fn.transcript_to_text.html)- to_ - text
- The transcript as Markdown-ish text (user/assistant/system/diff/tool lines;
reasoning and stats are omitted). Used by `/copy all`and`/export`.
- [turn_](https://docs.rs/fn.turn_stats_line.html)- stats_ - line
- The per-turn stats line both frontends append after a completed turn
(`✓ N tok · tok/s · elapsed · ttft · ctx`).`None`when the turn produced nothing measurable.`ttft_secs`is time-to-first-token; the token rate is measured from the first token, not the request start.
- [walk_](https://docs.rs/fn.walk_files.html)- files
- Collect relative file paths under `root`for`@file`completion. In a git repo, honors`.gitignore`/`.ignore`(and parents/global) +`.git/info/exclude`via the`ignore`crate; outside one, falls back to a manual walk that skips known VCS/build and hidden directories.
- [walk_](https://docs.rs/fn.walk_files_gitignore.html)- files_ - gitignore
- Gitignore-aware walk (ripgrep’s walker).
- [watch_](https://docs.rs/fn.watch_config.html)- config
- Watch the user config file, invoking `on_change`(from a background thread/task) on every modification — the unified hot-reload source for both frontends. Uses an OS-level watcher (inotify/FSEvents/…) on the config’s parent directory (so atomic saves via rename are caught) and falls back to 2s mtime polling when a watcher can’t be created. The callback should just ping the frontend’s channel; dedup (e.g. ignoring self-inflicted writes from persisting a setting) is the receiver’s job.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [HlLine](https://docs.rs/type.HlLine.html)
- One highlighted line: `(style, text)`runs. Text keeps syntect’s trailing newline (frontends trim as their renderer needs).
- [Line](https://docs.rs/type.LineFuture.html)- Future
- A future producing a system line to display (empty = show nothing). The host spawns it on its runtime and pipes the result to its transcript.
- [Rgb](https://docs.rs/type.Rgb.html)
- An RGB triple resolved from a theme.

# hrdr_editor - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hrdr-editor/0.2.1/hrdr_editor/

## Expand description

`hrdr-editor` — the FSM-agnostic editing seam.

The rest of hrdr talks only to the [ EditorEngine](https://docs.rs/trait.EditorEngine.html) trait — never to vim
types. The concrete

[wraps the hjkl engine and drives it through](https://docs.rs/struct.VimEngine.html)

`VimEngine``hjkl_vim::dispatch_input`. When hjkl’s pluggable-FSM work (epic
#265) lands a vscode/helix discipline, add a sibling `EditorEngine` impl
and the TUI swaps it in with zero churn — it reads `mode_label()` /
`is_insert()` (projected from hjkl’s FSM-agnostic `CoarseMode`), not
`VimMode`.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Editor](https://docs.rs/struct.EditorKey.html)- Key
- The seam’s renderer-agnostic key DTO — hjkl’s own toolkit-neutral
`Input { key, ctrl, alt, shift }`, re-exported so consumers never touch hjkl types directly. A key press with modifier flags. The vim engine reads modifiers directly off this struct (e.g.`input.ctrl && input.key == Key::Char('d')`).
- [Hrdr](https://docs.rs/struct.HrdrHost.html)- Host
- [Plain](https://docs.rs/struct.PlainEngine.html)- Engine
- A plain UTF-8 text buffer with a char-index cursor.
- [VimEngine](https://docs.rs/struct.VimEngine.html)
- The default discipline: hjkl’s vim FSM.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Editor](https://docs.rs/enum.EditorKeyCode.html)- KeyCode
- The seam’s renderer-agnostic key DTO — hjkl’s own toolkit-neutral
`Input { key, ctrl, alt, shift }`, re-exported so consumers never touch hjkl types directly. A key code, mirroring the subset of [`crossterm::event::KeyCode`] the vim engine actually consumes.`Null`is the conventional sentinel for “no input” (matching the previous`tui_textarea::Key`shape) so call sites can early-return on unsupported keys.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Editor](https://docs.rs/trait.EditorEngine.html)- Engine
- A pluggable editing discipline — the renderer-agnostic core of the seam.
- [TuiEditor](https://docs.rs/trait.TuiEditorEngine.html)- Engine
- What the TUI hosts: both halves of the seam.
- [TuiRender](https://docs.rs/trait.TuiRender.html)
- The terminal renderer half of the seam (ratatui). Kept out of
`EditorEngine`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [key_](https://docs.rs/fn.key_from_crossterm.html)- from_ - crossterm
- Convert a crossterm key event to the seam’s `EditorKey``None`for key-release events, which must not reach the engines (terminals reporting them would double keystrokes).

# hrdr_agent - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hrdr-agent/0.2.1/hrdr_agent/

## Expand description

`hrdr-agent` — the agentic loop.

Drives an OpenAI-compatible model through tool calls until a coding task is
complete: stream a turn, execute any requested tools, feed the results back,
repeat. Emits [ AgentEvent](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentEvent.html)s for a UI (or stdout) to render live.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.Agent.html)
- A running agent: model client + tools + conversation state.
- [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentConfig.html)- Config
- Agent configuration.
- [Checkpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckpointInfo.html)- Info
- One revertible checkpoint (a turn that changed files).
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileCheckpoints.html)- Checkpoints
- A disk-backed store of per-turn file pre-images.
- [Guardrail](https://docs.rs/struct.GuardrailConfig.html)- Config
- One user-defined shell guardrail from a `[[guardrails]]`config entry: commands matching`pattern`(a regex) are rejected with`message`. Applied on top of the built-in rules (`hrdr_tools::default_guardrails`).
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookConfig.html)- Config
- One post-edit hook from a `[[hooks]]`config entry: after tool`on`(`edit`,`write_file`, or`*`) successfully mutates a file matching`glob`, run shell command`run`(`{path}`is substituted). Formatters, mostly. Failures surface as warnings in the tool result, never as errors.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html)
- A single chat message. Used for both request and response — `content`is optional because assistant turns that only call tools carry no text.
- [Provider](https://docs.rs/struct.ProviderConfig.html)- Config
- A user-defined provider from `[providers.<name>]`in config.
- [Resolved](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolvedProvider.html)- Provider
- A fully-resolved provider preset.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.Session.html)
- A saved conversation.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionMeta.html)- Meta
- Lightweight directory listing entry.
- [Todo](https://docs.rs/struct.Todo.html)
- A single TODO item tracked by `todo_write`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Agent](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentEvent.html)- Event
- Events emitted as a turn progresses.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigValue.html)- Value
- A value to persist into the user config file.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/enum.MessageRole.html)- Role
- Message author role.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_AUTO_COMPACT.html)- AUTO_ - COMPACT
- Default auto-compaction trigger: 85% of the context window (leaves headroom so the next turn doesn’t overflow).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [builtin_](https://docs.rs/fn.builtin_provider.html)- provider
- Resolve a built-in provider name (case-insensitive).
- [config_](https://docs.rs/fn.config_dir.html)- dir
- `hrdr`’s config directory —- `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hrdr`, default- `~/.config/hrdr`(cross-platform via home-dir detection). Shared by- `config.toml`loading and the global- `AGENTS.md`lookup so the two can’t diverge.
- [config_](https://docs.rs/fn.config_file_path.html)- file_ - path
- Path to the user config file (`~/.config/hrdr/config.toml`), if`HOME`is set.
- [cwd_](https://docs.rs/fn.cwd_slug.html)- slug
- Slug for a working directory — the per-cwd subdirectory name. The full path
is flattened (e.g. `/home/me/Projects/foo`→`home-me-projects-foo`).
- [gather_](https://docs.rs/fn.gather_agent_docs.html)- agent_ - docs
- Collect project instructions from `AGENTS.md`files, walking from`cwd`up to the filesystem root, plus an optional global`~/.config/hrdr/AGENTS.md`. Less specific files (global, then ancestors) come first so nearer files override by appearing later. Returns`None`if nothing is found.
- [in_](https://docs.rs/fn.in_git_repo.html)- git_ - repo
- Whether `cwd`(or an ancestor) is inside a git repo.`.git`may be a directory (normal) or a file (worktrees/submodules).
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_sessions.html)- sessions
- List saved sessions across every working directory, newest first. Also
picks up legacy flat-layout files written directly under `sessions/`.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_env_bool.html)- env_ - bool
- Parse a boolean-ish env value; `None`(leave the current value) if it’s not one of the recognized on/off spellings. Parse a boolean setting from a config/CLI/env string, accepting the common spellings (`1`/`0`,`true`/`false`,`on`/`off`,`yes`/`no`, case-insensitive). Returns`None`for anything unrecognized so callers can leave the current value unchanged.
- [persist_](https://docs.rs/fn.persist_setting.html)- setting
- Set `key = value`in the user config file (creating it if needed), preserving existing keys, ordering, and comments. Returns the file path.
- [remove_](https://docs.rs/fn.remove_setting.html)- setting
- Remove `key`from the user config file (if present). Returns the file path.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_system.html)- system
- Render the agent system prompt for the given tool set and working directory.
`instructions`is the gathered AGENTS.md content (see`gather_agent_docs`
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_session.html)- session
- Resolve a `/resume`argument to`(id, Session)`. Looks in`cwd`’s directory first (by file id), then scans every directory — preferring the current`cwd`— matching the file id or the display`name`(case-insensitive, e.g. after`/rename`).
- [session_](https://docs.rs/fn.session_dir.html)- dir
- The per-cwd directory a session lives in.
- [sessions_](https://docs.rs/fn.sessions_dir.html)- dir
- `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hrdr/sessions`, or- `~/.local/share/hrdr/sessions`.
- [unique_](https://docs.rs/fn.unique_session_id.html)- session_ - id
- A collision-free file id (within `cwd`’s directory) derived from`name`: the slug, then`slug-2`,`slug-3`, … if files already exist.

# sandogasa_meetbot - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sandogasa-meetbot/0.15.3/sandogasa_meetbot/

## Expand description

HTTP client for [meetbot.fedoraproject.org](https://meetbot.fedoraproject.org/)’s
meeting search endpoint.

Meetbot exposes a single lightweight JSON endpoint for the “Search for conversations” UI in its web frontend. This crate wraps that endpoint behind a typed client.

```
use sandogasa_meetbot::Meetbot;
let client = Meetbot::new();
for meeting in client.search("centos-hyperscale-sig")? {
    println!("{} {}", meeting.datetime, meeting.summary_url);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_BASE_URL.html)- BASE_ - URL
- Default production base URL for meetbot’s web frontend.
- [PUBLIC_](https://docs.rs/constant.PUBLIC_ARTEFACT_BASE.html)- ARTEFACT_ - BASE
- Default base URL used for public meeting artefacts (log /
summary HTML). Distinct from the web frontend: the JSON
endpoint returns URLs on `meetbot-raw.fedoraproject.org`, but users typically want to link to the public-facing`meetbot.fedoraproject.org`host instead.`Meetbot::search`applies this rewrite.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [dedup_](https://docs.rs/fn.dedup_by_longest_log.html)- by_ - longest_ - log
- Collapse same-day duplicates in a meeting list by keeping
the entry whose `logs_url`is the largest, as a rough proxy for “the meeting that actually happened” when`!startmeeting`was run multiple times (on the same channel, or across overlapping channels) on a single day.`on_warning`is invoked once per collapsed group with`(winner, dropped)`so the caller can surface it to the user.

# camel_component_api - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camel-component-api/0.22.0/camel_component_api/

## Expand description

camel-component-api — traits and types for building Camel components.

Provides the core abstractions (`Component`, `Endpoint`, `Consumer`, `Producer`)
that every rust-camel component implements. Also re-exports commonly-used types
from `camel-api` and `camel-endpoint` for component convenience.

Main types: `Component`, `Endpoint`, `Consumer`, `ProducerContext`, `ExchangeEnvelope`, `ComponentBundle`, `PollingConsumer`.
Main modules: `component`, `endpoint`, `consumer`, `producer`, `registrar`.

# camel_language_rhai - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camel-language-rhai/0.22.0/camel_language_rhai/

## Expand description

camel-language-rhai — Rhai script language for Camel Rust.

Main types: `RhaiLanguage`, `RhaiExpression`, `RhaiPredicate`, `RhaiMutatingExpression`.
Scripts have access to `body`, `headers`, `header()`, `set_header()`, `property()`, `set_property()`.

[§](https://docs.rs#resource-limits)Resource Limits

Scripts are bounded by configurable limits sourced from `[languages.rhai.limits]`
in `Camel.toml`. When absent, the rust-camel runtime defaults apply:

| Limit | Default |
|---|---|
| `max-operations` | 100,000 |
| `max-string-size` | 1 MiB |
| `max-array-size` | 10,000 elements |
| `max-map-size` | 10,000 entries |
| `max-expression-depth` | 64 |
| `max-function-expression-depth` | 32 |
| `execution-timeout-ms` | 5,000 |

Every limit is `Option<_>`; `None` means “use rust-camel runtime default” (no
default-lie per ADR-0011).

[§](https://docs.rs#covered-threats)Covered threats

- Infinite loops (`loop {}`) — trip`max-operations`and`execution-timeout-ms`(whichever fires first).
- Oversized allocations — strings, arrays, maps each have size caps.
- Pathological nesting — expression and function-expression depths are bounded.

[§](https://docs.rs#timeout-caveat)Timeout caveat

`execution-timeout-ms` wraps `eval_with_scope` in `tokio::time::timeout` +
`spawn_blocking`. When the timeout fires, the route future resolves to an
error, but the blocking thread may continue executing until the script
trips `max-operations` or finishes. This is the same partial-mitigation
caveat shared with the Boa engine.

[§](https://docs.rs#sandboxing)Sandboxing

Rhai scripts **cannot access the host filesystem, network APIs, or Rhai
module loading**. This sandbox is **unconditional** — there is no config
opt-out.

Two structural layers enforce this:

- **Compile time**— the Rhai- `no_module`cargo feature (see root- `Cargo.toml`) disables module loading across the entire crate graph.
- **Runtime**— engines are built via- `Engine::new_raw()`plus an explicit- `StandardPackage`registration. Unlike- `Engine::new()`, this does not install a- `FileModuleResolver`.

Additionally, `eval` and `import` are registered as disabled symbols as
defense in depth (no-op safe if symbols are absent). If a future Rhai
package were to re-introduce module loading or dynamic evaluation, these
symbols would still be blocked to user scripts.

What the sandbox is **not**:

- It is not a CPU/memory cap. Those are separate resource limits; see rc-bpx.
- It does not block timing APIs (`sleep`,`timestamp`). Those remain part of`StandardPackage`; CPU/time-based DoS is covered by rc-bpx resource limits.
- It is not a side-channel defense (cache timing, memory layout). Out of scope.

If your integration genuinely needs filesystem or network access from a
route script, use the explicit Camel components (`file:`, `http:`) with
their own runtime policies — do not attempt to bypass this sandbox.

[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

- Resource limits (max operations, string/array/map sizes, expression
depths) are enforced as denial-of-service protection, not as a sandbox.
They are configurable — see [# Resource Limits](https://docs.rs#resource-limits)above.
- The `body`variable is always a string. Structured access to JSON/XML bodies requires explicit parsing within the script using Rhai’s built-in map/array types.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Rhai](https://docs.rs/struct.RhaiLanguage.html)- Language
- Rhai scripting language for rust-camel.

# ratatui-widgets 0.3.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2

# Ratatui Widgets

**ratatui-widgets** contains all the widgets that were previously part of the [Ratatui](https://crates.io/crates/ratatui) crate.
It is meant to be used in conjunction with `ratatui`, which provides the core functionality for
building terminal user interfaces.

Most applications shouldn't need to depend directly on `ratatui-widgets`, `ratatui` crate
re-exports all the widgets from this crate. However, if you are building a widget library that
internally uses these widgets, or if you prefer finer grained dependencies, you may want to
depend on this crate rather than transitively through the `ratatui` crate.

Previously, a crate named `ratatui-widgets` was published with some formative ideas about an
eventual Ratatui framework. That crate has now moved to [tui-framework-experiment](https://crates.io/crates/tui-framework-experiment), pending a
new name.

## Installation

Run the following command to add this crate to your project:

```
```
## Available Widgets

- `BarChart`
- `Block`
- `calendar::Monthly`
- `Canvas`
- `Chart`
- `Clear`
- `Fill`
- `Gauge`
- `LineGauge`
- `List`
- `RatatuiLogo`
- `RatatuiMascot`
- `Paragraph`
- `Scrollbar`
- `Sparkline`
- `Table`
- `Tabs`

All these widgets are re-exported directly under `ratatui::widgets` in the `ratatui` crate.

## Crate Organization

`ratatui-widgets` is part of the Ratatui workspace that was modularized in version 0.30.0.
This crate contains all the built-in widget implementations that were previously part of the
main `ratatui` crate.

**When to use  ratatui-widgets:**

- Building widget libraries that need to compose with built-in widgets
- You want finer-grained dependencies and only need specific widgets
- Creating custom widgets that extend or wrap the built-in ones

**When to use the main **

`ratatui` crate:- Building applications (recommended - includes everything you need)
- You want the convenience of having all widgets available

For detailed information about the workspace organization, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue or submit a pull request on GitHub. For more
details on contributing, please see the [CONTRIBUTING](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License. See the [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) file for details.

[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! **ratatui-widgets** contains all the widgets that were previously part of the [Ratatui] crate.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! It is meant to be used in conjunction with `ratatui`, which provides the core functionality for
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! building terminal user interfaces.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! [Ratatui]: https://crates.io/crates/ratatui
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! Most applications shouldn't need to depend directly on `ratatui-widgets`, `ratatui` crate
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! re-exports all the widgets from this crate. However, if you are building a widget library that
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! internally uses these widgets, or if you prefer finer grained dependencies, you may want to
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! depend on this crate rather than transitively through the `ratatui` crate.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! Previously, a crate named `ratatui-widgets` was published with some formative ideas about an
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! eventual Ratatui framework. That crate has now moved to [tui-framework-experiment], pending a
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! new name.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! [tui-framework-experiment]: https://crates.io/crates/tui-framework-experiment
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! # Installation
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! Run the following command to add this crate to your project:
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! ```sh
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! cargo add ratatui-widgets
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! ```
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! # Available Widgets
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! - [`BarChart`]: displays multiple datasets as bars with optional grouping.
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! - [`Block`]: a basic widget that draws a block with optional borders, titles, and styles.
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! - [`calendar::Monthly`]: displays a single month.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! - [`Canvas`]: draws arbitrary shapes using drawing characters.
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! - [`Chart`]: displays multiple datasets as lines or scatter graphs.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! - [`Clear`]: clears the area it occupies. Useful to render over previously drawn widgets.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! - [`Fill`]: paints every cell in its area with a single repeated symbol and style.
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! - [`Gauge`]: displays progress percentage using block characters.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! - [`LineGauge`]: displays progress as a line.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! - [`List`]: displays a list of items and allows selection.
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! - [`RatatuiLogo`]: displays the Ratatui logo.
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! - [`RatatuiMascot`]: displays the Ratatui mascot.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! - [`Paragraph`]: displays a paragraph of optionally styled and wrapped text.
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! - [`Scrollbar`]: displays a scrollbar.
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! - [`Sparkline`]: displays a single dataset as a sparkline.
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! - [`Table`]: displays multiple rows and columns in a grid and allows selection.
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! - [`Tabs`]: displays a tab bar and allows selection.
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! [`BarChart`]: crate::barchart::BarChart

[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! # Crate Organization
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! `ratatui-widgets` is part of the Ratatui workspace that was modularized in version 0.30.0.
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! This crate contains all the built-in widget implementations that were previously part of the
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! main `ratatui` crate.
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! **When to use `ratatui-widgets`:**
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! - Building widget libraries that need to compose with built-in widgets
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! - You want finer-grained dependencies and only need specific widgets
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! - Creating custom widgets that extend or wrap the built-in ones
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! **When to use the main [`ratatui`] crate:**
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! - Building applications (recommended - includes everything you need)
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! - You want the convenience of having all widgets available
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! For detailed information about the workspace organization, see [ARCHITECTURE.md].
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! [`ratatui`]: https://crates.io/crates/ratatui
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! [ARCHITECTURE.md]: https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
