# BarChart in ratatui_widgets::barchart - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/barchart/struct.BarChart.html

`pub struct BarChart<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A chart showing values as [bars](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html).

Here is a possible `BarChart` output.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│                             ████│
│                        ▅▅▅▅ ████│
│            ▇▇▇▇        ████ ████│
│     ▄▄▄▄   ████ ████   ████ ████│
│▆10▆ █20█   █50█ █40█   █60█ █90█│
│ B1   B2     B1   B2     B1   B2 │
│ Group1      Group2      Group3  │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```
A `BarChart` is composed of a set of [ Bar](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html) which can be set via

[. Bars can be styled globally (](https://docs.rs/struct.BarChart.html#method.data)

`BarChart::data`[) or individually (](https://docs.rs/struct.BarChart.html#method.bar_style)

`BarChart::bar_style`[). There are other methods available to style even more precisely. See](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html#method.style)

`Bar::style`[to find out about each bar component.](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html)

`Bar`The `BarChart` widget can also show groups of bars via [ BarGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.BarGroup.html).
A

[is a set of](https://docs.rs/struct.BarGroup.html)

`BarGroup`[, multiple can be added to a](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html)

`Bar``BarChart` using
[multiple time as demonstrated in the example below.](https://docs.rs/struct.BarChart.html#method.data)

`BarChart::data`The chart can have a [ Direction](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/direction/enum.Direction.html) (by default the bars are

[). This is set using](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/direction/enum.Direction.html#variant.Vertical)

`Vertical`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.BarChart.html#method.direction)

`BarChart::direction`Note: this is the only widget that doesn’t implement `Widget` for `&T` because the current
implementation modifies the internal state of self. This will be fixed in the future.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The following example creates a `BarChart` with two groups of bars.
The first group is added by an array slice (`&[(&str, u64)]`).
The second group is added by a [ BarGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.BarGroup.html) instance.

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::{Bar, BarChart, BarGroup, Block};
BarChart::default()
    .block(Block::bordered().title("BarChart"))
    .bar_width(3)
    .bar_gap(1)
    .group_gap(3)
    .bar_style(Style::new().yellow().on_red())
    .value_style(Style::new().red().bold())
    .label_style(Style::new().white())
    .data(&[("A0", 0), ("A1", 2), ("A2", 4), ("A3", 3)])
    .data(BarGroup::new([
        Bar::with_label("B0", 10),
        Bar::with_label("B2", 20),
    ]))
    .max(4);
```
For simpler usages, you can also create a `BarChart` simply by

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Bar, BarChart};
BarChart::new([Bar::with_label("A", 10), Bar::with_label("B", 20)]);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new vertical `BarChart` widget with the given bars.

The `bars` parameter accepts any type that can be converted into a `Vec<Bar>`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use ratatui::layout::Direction;
use ratatui::widgets::{Bar, BarChart};
BarChart::new(vec![Bar::with_label("A", 10), Bar::with_label("B", 10)]);
```
Creates a new `BarChart` widget with a vertical direction.

This function is equivalent to `BarChart::new()`.

Creates a new `BarChart` widget with a group of bars.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Bar, BarChart, BarGroup};
BarChart::grouped(vec![
    BarGroup::with_label(
        "Group 1",
        vec![Bar::with_label("A", 10), Bar::with_label("B", 20)],
    ),
    BarGroup::with_label(
        "Group 2",
        [Bar::with_label("C", 30), Bar::with_label("D", 40)],
    ),
]);
```
Add group of bars to the `BarChart`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

The following example creates a `BarChart` with two groups of bars.
The first group is added by an array slice (`&[(&str, u64)]`).
The second group is added by a [ BarGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.BarGroup.html) instance.

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Bar, BarChart, BarGroup};
BarChart::default()
    .data(&[("B0", 0), ("B1", 2), ("B2", 4), ("B3", 3)])
    .data(BarGroup::new([
        Bar::with_label("A", 10),
        Bar::with_label("B", 20),
    ]));
```
Set the value necessary for a [ Bar](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html) to reach the maximum height.

If not set, the maximum value in the data is taken as reference.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

This example shows the default behavior when `max` is not set.
The maximum value in the dataset is taken (here, `100`).

```
use ratatui::widgets::BarChart;
BarChart::default().data(&[("foo", 1), ("bar", 2), ("baz", 100)]);
// Renders
//     █
//     █
// f b b
```
This example shows a custom max value.
The maximum height being `2`, `bar` & `baz` render as the max.

```
use ratatui::widgets::BarChart;
BarChart::default()
    .data(&[("foo", 1), ("bar", 2), ("baz", 100)])
    .max(2);
// Renders
//   █ █
// █ █ █
// f b b
```
Set the default style of the bar.

`style` accepts any type that is convertible to [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) (e.g.

[,](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`It is also possible to set individually the style of each [ Bar](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html).
In this case the default style will be patched by the individual style

Set the gap between each bar.

If not set, this defaults to `1`.
The bar label will never be larger than the bar itself, even if the gap is sufficient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

This shows two bars with a gap of `3`. Notice the labels will always stay under the bar.

```
use ratatui::widgets::BarChart;
BarChart::default()
    .data(&[("foo", 1), ("bar", 2)])
    .bar_gap(3);
// Renders
//     █
// █   █
// f   b
```

# Block in ratatui_widgets::block - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/block/struct.Block.html

`pub struct Block<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget that renders borders, titles, and padding around other widgets.

A `Block` is a foundational widget that creates visual containers by drawing borders around an
area. It serves as a wrapper or frame for other widgets, providing structure and visual
separation in terminal UIs. Most built-in widgets in Ratatui use a pattern where they accept an
optional `Block` parameter that wraps the widget’s content.

When a widget renders with a block, the widget’s style is applied first, then the block’s style, and finally the widget’s content is rendered within the inner area calculated by the block. This layered approach allows for flexible styling where the block can provide background colors, borders, and padding while the inner widget handles its own content styling.

Multiple blocks can be nested within each other. The [ Block::inner](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.inner) method calculates the area
available for content after accounting for borders, titles, and padding, making it easy to nest
blocks or position widgets within a block’s boundaries.

[§](https://docs.rs#constructor-methods)Constructor Methods

- `Block::new`
- `Block::bordered`

[§](https://docs.rs#border-configuration)Border Configuration

- `Block::borders`
- `Block::border_style`
- `Block::border_type`
- `Block::border_set`- `border::Set`
- `Block::merge_borders`

[§](https://docs.rs#title-configuration)Title Configuration

- `Block::title`
- `Block::title_top`
- `Block::title_bottom`
- `Block::title_alignment`
- `Block::title_style`
- `Block::title_position`

[§](https://docs.rs#styling-and-layout)Styling and Layout

- `Block::style`
- `Block::shadow`
- `Block::padding`
- `Block::inner`

[§](https://docs.rs#title-behavior)Title Behavior

You can add multiple titles to a block, and they will be rendered with spaces separating titles that share the same position or alignment. When both centered and non-centered titles exist, the centered space is calculated based on the full width of the block.

Titles are set using the `.title`, `.title_top`, and `.title_bottom` methods. These methods
accept a string or any type that can be converted into a [ Line](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/line/struct.Line.html), such as a string slice,

`String`, or a vector of [s. To control the alignment of a title (left, center, right), pass a](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html)

`Span``Line` with the desired alignment, e.g. `Line::from("Title").centered()`.By default, `.title` places the title at the top of the block, but you can use `.title_top` or
`.title_bottom` to explicitly set the position. The default alignment for all titles can be set
with [ Block::title_alignment](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_alignment), and the default position for all titles can be set with

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_position)

`Block::title_position`Note that prior to `v0.30.0`, the `block::Title` struct was used to create titles. This struct
has been removed. The new recommended approach is to use [ Line](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/line/struct.Line.html) with a specific alignment for
the title’s content and the

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_top)

`Block::title_top`[methods for positioning.](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_bottom)

`Block::title_bottom`Titles avoid being rendered in corners when borders are present, but will align to edges when no border exists on that side:

```
┌With at least a left border───
Without left border───
```
[§](https://docs.rs#nesting-widgets-with-inner)Nesting Widgets with `inner`

The [ Block::inner](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.inner) method computes the area inside the block after accounting for borders,
titles, and padding. This allows you to nest widgets inside a block by rendering the block
first, then rendering other widgets in the returned inner area.

For example, you can nest a block inside another block:

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
let outer_block = Block::bordered().title("Outer");
let inner_block = Block::bordered().title("Inner");
let outer_area = frame.area();
let inner_area = outer_block.inner(outer_area);
frame.render_widget(outer_block, outer_area);
frame.render_widget(inner_block, inner_area);
```
You can also use the standard [ Layout](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/layout/struct.Layout.html) functionality to further subdivide the inner area and
lay out multiple widgets inside a block.

[§](https://docs.rs#integration-with-other-widgets)Integration with Other Widgets

Most widgets in Ratatui accept a block parameter. For example, [ Paragraph](https://docs.rs/paragraph/struct.Paragraph.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/list/struct.List.html)

`List`[, and other widgets can be wrapped with a block:](https://docs.rs/table/struct.Table.html)

`Table````
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Paragraph};
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Hello, world!").block(Block::bordered().title("My Paragraph"));
```
This pattern allows widgets to focus on their content while blocks handle the visual framing.

[§](https://docs.rs#styling)Styling

Styles are applied in a specific order: first the block’s base style, then border styles, then title styles, and finally any content widget styles. This layered approach allows for flexible styling where outer styles provide defaults that inner styles can override.

`Block` implements [ Stylize](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/stylize/trait.Stylize.html), allowing you to use style
shorthand methods:

```
use ratatui::style::Stylize;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
let block = Block::bordered().red().on_white().bold();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a simple bordered block:

```
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
let block = Block::bordered().title("My Block");
```
Create a block with custom border styling:

```
use ratatui::style::{Color, Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, BorderType};
let block = Block::bordered()
    .title("Styled Block")
    .border_type(BorderType::Rounded)
    .border_style(Style::new().cyan())
    .style(Style::new().on_black());
```
Use a block to wrap another widget:

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Paragraph};
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Hello, world!").block(Block::bordered().title("Greeting"));
```
Add multiple titles with different alignments:

```
use ratatui::text::Line;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
let block = Block::bordered()
    .title_top(Line::from("Left").left_aligned())
    .title_top(Line::from("Center").centered())
    .title_top(Line::from("Right").right_aligned())
    .title_bottom("Status: OK");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See Also

- [Block recipe](https://ratatui.rs/recipes/widgets/block/)- Visual examples and common patterns (on the ratatui website)
- [Collapse borders recipe](https://ratatui.rs/recipes/layout/collapse-borders/)- Techniques for creating seamless layouts (on the ratatui website)
- `MergeStrategy`

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Adds a title to the block using the default position.

The position of the title is determined by the `title_position` field of the block, which
defaults to `Top`. This can be changed using the [ Block::title_position](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_position) method. For
explicit positioning, use

[or](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_top)

`Block::title_top`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_bottom)

`Block::title_bottom`The `title` function allows you to add a title to the block. You can call this function
multiple times to add multiple titles.

Each title will be rendered with a single space separating titles that are in the same position or alignment. When both centered and non-centered titles are rendered, the centered space is calculated based on the full width of the block, rather than the leftover width.

You can provide any type that can be converted into [ Line](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/line/struct.Line.html) including: strings, string
slices (

`&str`), borrowed strings (`Cow<str>`), [spans](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html), or vectors of

[spans](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html)(

`Vec<Span>`).By default, the titles will avoid being rendered in the corners of the block but will align against the left or right edge of the block if there is no border on that edge. The following demonstrates this behavior, notice the second title is one character off to the left.

```
┌With at least a left border───
Without left border───
```
Note: If the block is too small and multiple titles overlap, the border might get cut off at a corner.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

See the [Block example](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/blob/main/examples/README.md#block) for a visual representation of how the various borders and styles
look when rendered.

The following example demonstrates:

- Default title alignment
- Multiple titles (notice “Center” is centered according to the full with of the block, not the leftover space)
- Two titles with the same alignment (notice the left titles are separated)

```
use ratatui::text::Line;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
Block::bordered()
    .title("Title")
    .title(Line::from("Left").left_aligned())
    .title(Line::from("Right").right_aligned())
    .title(Line::from("Center").centered());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-1)See also

Titles attached to a block can have default behaviors. See

[§](https://docs.rs#history)History

In previous releases of Ratatui this method accepted `Into<Title>` instead of
[ Into<Line>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html). We found that storing the position in the block and the alignment in the
line better reflects the intended use of the block and its titles. See

[https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/issues/738](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/issues/738)for more information.

Adds a title to the top of the block.

You can provide any type that can be converted into [ Line](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/line/struct.Line.html) including: strings, string
slices (

`&str`), borrowed strings (`Cow<str>`), [spans](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html), or vectors of

[spans](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html)(

`Vec<Span>`).[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ratatui::{ widgets::Block, text::Line };
Block::bordered()
    .title_top("Left1") // By default in the top left corner
    .title_top(Line::from("Left2").left_aligned())
    .title_top(Line::from("Right").right_aligned())
    .title_top(Line::from("Center").centered());
// Renders
// ┌Left1─Left2───Center─────────Right┐
// │                                  │
// └──────────────────────────────────┘
```
Adds a title to the bottom of the block.

You can provide any type that can be converted into [ Line](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/line/struct.Line.html) including: strings, string
slices (

`&str`), borrowed strings (`Cow<str>`), [spans](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html), or vectors of

[spans](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html)(

`Vec<Span>`).[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use ratatui::{ widgets::Block, text::Line };
Block::bordered()
    .title_bottom("Left1") // By default in the top left corner
    .title_bottom(Line::from("Left2").left_aligned())
    .title_bottom(Line::from("Right").right_aligned())
    .title_bottom(Line::from("Center").centered());
// Renders
// ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
// │                                  │
// └Left1─Left2───Center─────────Right┘
```

Sets the default [ Alignment](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/alignment/type.Alignment.html) for all block titles.

Titles that explicitly set an [ Alignment](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/alignment/type.Alignment.html) will ignore this.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

This example aligns all titles in the center except the “right” title which explicitly sets
[ Alignment::Right](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/alignment/type.Alignment.html#variant.Right).

use ratatui::layout::Alignment;
use ratatui::text::Line;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
Block::bordered()
    .title_alignment(Alignment::Center)
    // This title won't be aligned in the center
    .title(Line::from("right").right_aligned())
    .title("foo")
    .title("bar");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/block.rs.html#494-497)#### pub const fn [title_position](https://docs.rs#method.title_position)(self, position: [TitlePosition](https://docs.rs/enum.TitlePosition.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/block.rs.html#494-497)

#### pub const fn [title_position](https://docs.rs#method.title_position)(self, position: [TitlePosition](https://docs.rs/enum.TitlePosition.html)) -> Self

Sets the default [ TitlePosition](https://docs.rs/enum.TitlePosition.html) for all block titles.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

This example positions all titles on the bottom by default. The “top” title explicitly sets
its position to `Top`, so it is not affected. The “foo” and “bar” titles will be positioned
at the bottom.

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, TitlePosition};
Block::bordered()
    .title_position(TitlePosition::Bottom)
    .title("foo") // will be at the bottom
    .title_top("top") // will be at the top
    .title("bar"); // will be at the bottom
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/block.rs.html#520-523)#### pub fn [border_style](https://docs.rs#method.border_style)<S: [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)>>(self, style: S) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/block.rs.html#520-523)

Defines the style of the borders.

This style is applied only to the areas covered by borders, and is applied to the block
after any [ Block::style](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.style) is applied.

See [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) for more information on how merging styles works.

`style` accepts any type that is convertible to [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) (e.g.

[,](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

This example shows a `Block` with blue borders.

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
Block::bordered().border_style(Style::new().blue());
```
Defines the style of the entire block.

This is the most generic [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) a block can receive, it will be merged with any other
more specific styles. Elements can be styled further with

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.title_style)

`Block::title_style`[, which will be applied on top of this style. If the block is used as a container for another widget (e.g. a](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.border_style)

`Block::border_style`[), then the style of the widget is generally applied before this style.](https://docs.rs/paragraph/struct.Paragraph.html)

`Paragraph`See [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) for more information on how merging styles works.

`style` accepts any type that is convertible to [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) (e.g.

[,](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
use ratatui::style::{Color, Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Paragraph};
let block = Block::new().style(Style::new().red().on_black());
// For border and title you can additionally apply styles on top of the block level style.
let block = Block::new()
    .style(Style::new().red().bold().italic())
    .border_style(Style::new().not_italic()) // will be red and bold
    .title_style(Style::new().not_bold()) // will be red and italic
    .title("Title");
// To style the inner widget, you can style the widget itself.
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Content")
    .block(block)
    .style(Style::new().white().not_bold()); // will be white, and italic
```
Defines which borders to display.

[ Borders](https://docs.rs/borders/struct.Borders.html) can also be styled with

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.border_style)

`Block::border_style`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html#method.border_type)

`Block::border_type`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

Display left and right borders.

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Borders};
Block::new().borders(Borders::LEFT | Borders::RIGHT);
```
To show all borders you can abbreviate this with `Block::bordered`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/block.rs.html#707-710)#### pub const fn [merge_borders](https://docs.rs#method.merge_borders)(self, strategy: [MergeStrategy](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/block.rs.html#707-710)

#### pub const fn [merge_borders](https://docs.rs#method.merge_borders)(self, strategy: [MergeStrategy](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html)) -> Self

Sets the block’s [ MergeStrategy](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html) for overlapping characters, defaulting to

[.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html#variant.Replace)

`Replace`Changing the strategy to [ Exact](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html#variant.Exact) or

[collapses border characters that intersect with any previously rendered borders.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html#variant.Fuzzy)

`Fuzzy`For more information and examples, see the [collapse borders recipe](https://ratatui.rs/recipes/layout/collapse-borders/) and [ MergeStrategy](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/merge/enum.MergeStrategy.html)
docs.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
use ratatui::symbols::merge::MergeStrategy;
// Given several blocks with plain borders (1)
Block::bordered();
// and other blocks with thick borders (2) which are rendered on top of the first
Block::bordered()
    .border_type(BorderType::Thick)
    .merge_borders(MergeStrategy::Exact);
```
Rendering these blocks with `MergeStrategy::Exact` or `MergeStrategy::Fuzzy` will collapse
the borders, resulting in a clean layout without connected borders.

```
┌───┐    ┌───┐  ┌───┲━━━┓┌───┐
│   │    │ 1 │  │   ┃   ┃│   │
│ 1 │    │ ┏━┿━┓│ 1 ┃ 2 ┃│ 1 │
│   │    │ ┃ │ ┃│   ┃   ┃│   │
└───╆━━━┓└─╂─┘ ┃└───┺━━━┛┢━━━┪
    ┃   ┃  ┃ 2 ┃         ┃   ┃
    ┃ 2 ┃  ┗━━━┛         ┃ 2 ┃
    ┃   ┃                ┃   ┃
    ┗━━━┛                ┗━━━┛
```
Adds a shadow behind the block.

The shadow is rendered using the block area plus the shadow’s configured offset.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-7)Example

```
use ratatui::layout::Offset;
use ratatui::style::Stylize;
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Shadow};
let block = Block::bordered().title("Popup").shadow(
    Shadow::dark_shade()
        .black()
        .on_white()
        .offset(Offset::new(2, 1)),
);
```
Computes the inner area of a block after subtracting space for borders, titles, and padding.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

Draw a block nested within another block

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
let outer_block = Block::bordered().title("Outer");
let inner_block = Block::bordered().title("Inner");
let outer_area = frame.area();
let inner_area = outer_block.inner(outer_area);
frame.render_widget(outer_block, outer_area);
frame.render_widget(inner_block, inner_area);
// Renders
// ┌Outer────────┐
// │┌Inner──────┐│
// ││           ││
// │└───────────┘│
// └─────────────┘
```

# Canvas in ratatui_widgets::canvas - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/canvas/struct.Canvas.html

`pub struct Canvas<'a, F>{ /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The Canvas widget provides a means to draw shapes (Lines, Rectangles, Circles, etc.) on a grid.

By default the grid is made of Braille patterns but you may change the marker to use a different
set of symbols. If your terminal or font does not support this unicode block, you will see
unicode replacement characters (�) instead of braille dots. The Braille patterns (as well the
octant character patterns) provide a more fine grained result with a 2x4 resolution per
character, but you might want to use a simple dot, block, or bar instead by calling the
[ marker](https://docs.rs#method.marker) method if your target environment does not support those symbols.

See [Unicode Braille Patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braille_Patterns) for more info.

The `Octant` marker is similar to the `Braille` marker but, instead of sparse dots, displays
densely packed and regularly spaced pseudo-pixels, without visible bands between rows and
columns. However, it uses characters that are not yet as widely supported as the Braille
unicode block.

The `Quadrant` and `Sextant` markers are in turn akin to the `Octant` marker, but with a 2x2
and 2x3 resolution, respectively.

The `HalfBlock` marker is useful when you want to draw shapes with a higher resolution than a
`CharGrid` but lower than a `PatternGrid`. This grid type supports a foreground and background
color for each terminal cell. This allows for more flexibility than the `PatternGrid` which
only supports a single foreground color for each 2x4 dots cell.

The Canvas widget is used by calling the [ Canvas::paint](https://docs.rs/struct.Canvas.html#method.paint) method and passing a closure that
will be used to draw on the canvas. The closure will be passed a

[object that can be used to draw shapes on the canvas.](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`The [ Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html) object provides a

[method that can be used to draw shapes on the canvas. The](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.draw)

`Context::draw`[method can be used to save the current state of the canvas and start a new layer. This is useful if you want to draw multiple shapes on the canvas in specific order. The](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.layer)

`Context::layer`[object also provides a](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)

`Context`[method that can be used to print text on the canvas. Note that the text is always printed on top of the canvas and is not affected by the layers.](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.print)

`Context::print`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::style::Color;
use ratatui::widgets::Block;
use ratatui::widgets::canvas::{Canvas, Line, Map, MapResolution, Rectangle};
Canvas::default()
    .block(Block::bordered().title("Canvas"))
    .x_bounds([-180.0, 180.0])
    .y_bounds([-90.0, 90.0])
    .paint(|ctx| {
        ctx.draw(&Map {
            resolution: MapResolution::High,
            color: Color::White,
        });
        ctx.layer();
        ctx.draw(&Line {
            x1: 0.0,
            y1: 10.0,
            x2: 10.0,
            y2: 10.0,
            color: Color::White,
        });
        ctx.draw(&Rectangle {
            x: 10.0,
            y: 20.0,
            width: 10.0,
            height: 10.0,
            color: Color::Red,
        });
    });
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Define the viewport of the canvas.

If you were to “zoom” to a certain part of the world you may want to choose different bounds.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

Define the viewport of the canvas.

If you were to “zoom” to a certain part of the world you may want to choose different bounds.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

Change the type of points used to draw the shapes.

By default the [ Braille](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.Braille) patterns are used as they provide a more fine grained result,
but you might want to use the simple

[or](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.Dot)

`Dot`[instead if the targeted terminal does not support those symbols.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.Block)

`Block`The [ HalfBlock](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.HalfBlock) marker is useful when you want to draw shapes with a higher resolution
than with a grid of characters (e.g. with

[or](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.Block)

`Block`[) but lower than with](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.Dot)

`Dot`[. This grid type supports a foreground and background color for each terminal cell. This allows for more flexibility than the](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/marker/enum.Marker.html#variant.Braille)

`Braille``PatternGrid` which only supports a single
foreground color for each 2x4 dots cell.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use ratatui::symbols;
use ratatui::widgets::canvas::Canvas;
Canvas::default()
    .marker(symbols::Marker::Braille)
    .paint(|ctx| {});
Canvas::default()
    .marker(symbols::Marker::HalfBlock)
    .paint(|ctx| {});
Canvas::default()
    .marker(symbols::Marker::Dot)
    .paint(|ctx| {});
Canvas::default()
    .marker(symbols::Marker::Block)
    .paint(|ctx| {});
```

# Chart in ratatui_widgets::chart - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/chart/struct.Chart.html

`pub struct Chart<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget to plot one or more [ Dataset](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html) in a cartesian coordinate system

To use this widget, start by creating one or more [ Dataset](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html). With it, you can set the

[data points](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html#method.data), the

[name](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html#method.name)or the

[chart type](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html#method.graph_type). See

[for a complete documentation of what is possible.](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html)

`Dataset`Then, you’ll usually want to configure the [ Axis](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html). Axis

[titles](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html#method.title),

[bounds](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html#method.bounds)and

[labels](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html#method.labels)can be configured on both axis. See

[for a complete documentation of what is possible.](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html)

`Axis`Finally, you can pass all of that to the `Chart` via [ Chart::new](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.new),

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.x_axis)

`Chart::x_axis`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.y_axis)

`Chart::y_axis`Additionally, `Chart` allows configuring the legend [position](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.legend_position) and
[hiding constraints](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.hidden_legend_constraints).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::symbols;
use ratatui::widgets::{Axis, Block, Chart, Dataset, GraphType};
// Create the datasets to fill the chart with
let datasets = vec![
    // Scatter chart
    Dataset::default()
        .name("data1")
        .marker(symbols::Marker::Dot)
        .graph_type(GraphType::Scatter)
        .style(Style::default().cyan())
        .data(&[(0.0, 5.0), (1.0, 6.0), (1.5, 6.434)]),
    // Line chart
    Dataset::default()
        .name("data2")
        .marker(symbols::Marker::Braille)
        .graph_type(GraphType::Line)
        .style(Style::default().magenta())
        .data(&[(4.0, 5.0), (5.0, 8.0), (7.66, 13.5)]),
];
// Create the X axis and define its properties
let x_axis = Axis::default()
    .title("X Axis".red())
    .style(Style::default().white())
    .bounds([0.0, 10.0])
    .labels(["0.0", "5.0", "10.0"]);
// Create the Y axis and define its properties
let y_axis = Axis::default()
    .title("Y Axis".red())
    .style(Style::default().white())
    .bounds([0.0, 10.0])
    .labels(["0.0", "5.0", "10.0"]);
// Create the chart and link all the parts together
let chart = Chart::new(datasets)
    .block(Block::new().title("Chart"))
    .x_axis(x_axis)
    .y_axis(y_axis);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a chart with the given [datasets](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html)

A chart can render multiple datasets.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

This creates a simple chart with one `Dataset`

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Chart, Dataset};
let data_points = vec![];
let chart = Chart::new(vec![Dataset::default().data(&data_points)]);
```
This creates a chart with multiple [ Dataset](https://docs.rs/struct.Dataset.html)s

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Chart, Dataset};
let data_points = vec![];
let data_points2 = vec![];
let chart = Chart::new(vec![
    Dataset::default().data(&data_points),
    Dataset::default().data(&data_points2),
]);
```
Sets the X `Axis`

The default is an empty [ Axis](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html), i.e. only a line.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Axis, Chart};
let chart = Chart::new(vec![]).x_axis(
    Axis::default()
        .title("X Axis")
        .bounds([0.0, 20.0])
        .labels(["0", "20"]),
);
```
Sets the Y `Axis`

The default is an empty [ Axis](https://docs.rs/struct.Axis.html), i.e. only a line.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Axis, Chart};
let chart = Chart::new(vec![]).y_axis(
    Axis::default()
        .title("Y Axis")
        .bounds([0.0, 20.0])
        .labels(["0", "20"]),
);
```
Sets the constraints used to determine whether the legend should be shown or not.

The tuple’s first constraint is used for the width and the second for the height. If the
legend takes more space than what is allowed by any constraint, the legend is hidden.
[ Constraint::Min](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/constraint/enum.Constraint.html#variant.Min) is an exception and will always show the legend.

If this is not set, the default behavior is to hide the legend if it is greater than 25% of the chart, either horizontally or vertically.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

Hide the legend when either its width is greater than 33% of the total widget width or if its height is greater than 25% of the total widget height.

```
use ratatui::layout::Constraint;
use ratatui::widgets::Chart;
let constraints = (Constraint::Ratio(1, 3), Constraint::Ratio(1, 4));
let chart = Chart::new(vec![]).hidden_legend_constraints(constraints);
```
Always show the legend, note the second constraint doesn’t matter in this case since the first one is always true.

```
use ratatui::layout::Constraint;
use ratatui::widgets::Chart;
let constraints = (Constraint::Min(0), Constraint::Ratio(1, 4));
let chart = Chart::new(vec![]).hidden_legend_constraints(constraints);
```
Always hide the legend. Note this can be accomplished more explicitly by passing `None` to
[ Chart::legend_position](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.legend_position).

```
use ratatui::layout::Constraint;
use ratatui::widgets::Chart;
let constraints = (Constraint::Length(0), Constraint::Ratio(1, 4));
let chart = Chart::new(vec![]).hidden_legend_constraints(constraints);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/chart.rs.html#745-748)#### pub const fn [legend_position](https://docs.rs#method.legend_position)(self, position: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[LegendPosition](https://docs.rs/enum.LegendPosition.html)>) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/chart.rs.html#745-748)

#### pub const fn [legend_position](https://docs.rs#method.legend_position)(self, position: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[LegendPosition](https://docs.rs/enum.LegendPosition.html)>) -> Self

Sets the position of a legend or hide it

The default is [ LegendPosition::TopRight](https://docs.rs/enum.LegendPosition.html#variant.TopRight).

If [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) is given, hide the legend even if

[determines it should be shown. In contrast, if](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.hidden_legend_constraints)

`hidden_legend_constraints``Some(...)` is given, [might still decide whether to show the legend or not.](https://docs.rs/struct.Chart.html#method.hidden_legend_constraints)

`hidden_legend_constraints`See [ LegendPosition](https://docs.rs/enum.LegendPosition.html) for all available positions.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

Show the legend on the top left corner.

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Chart, LegendPosition};
let chart: Chart = Chart::new(vec![]).legend_position(Some(LegendPosition::TopLeft));
```
Hide the legend altogether

```
use ratatui::widgets::{Chart, LegendPosition};
let chart = Chart::new(vec![]).legend_position(None);
```

# Clear in ratatui_widgets::clear - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/clear/struct.Clear.html

`pub struct Clear;`## Expand description

A widget to clear/reset a certain area to allow overdrawing (e.g. for popups).

This widget **cannot be used to clear the terminal on the first render** as `ratatui` assumes
the render area is empty. Use `Terminal::clear` instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Clear};
fn draw_on_clear(f: &mut Frame, area: Rect) {
    let block = Block::bordered().title("Block");
    f.render_widget(Clear, area); // <- this will clear/reset the area first
    f.render_widget(block, area); // now render the block widget
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#popup-example)Popup Example

For a more complete example how to utilize `Clear` to realize popups see
the example `examples/popup.rs`

# Fill in ratatui_widgets::fill - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/fill/struct.Fill.html

`pub struct Fill<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget that fills its render area with a single repeated symbol and style.

[ Fill](https://docs.rs/struct.Fill.html) is a small building block for painting solid blocks of one symbol — backgrounds,
separators, scrollbar tracks, custom borders, etc. — without writing the nested loop
yourself. It composes naturally with the

[trait so the typical call site is a one-liner.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/stylize/trait.Stylize.html)

`Stylize`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::style::Stylize;
use ratatui::widgets::{Fill, Widget};
let fill = Fill::new("X").blue().bold();
fill.render(Rect::new(0, 0, 10, 3), &mut buf);
```
This renders as:

```
XXXXXXXXXX
XXXXXXXXXX
XXXXXXXXXX
```
[ Fill](https://docs.rs/struct.Fill.html) accepts anything that converts into a

[, so both string literals and owned](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html)

`Cow<str>`[s work:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`String````
use ratatui::widgets::Fill;
let _ = Fill::new("•");
let _ = Fill::new(String::from("•"));
```
Cells outside the buffer are silently clipped, mirroring the behavior of other widgets
such as [ Clear](https://docs.rs/clear/struct.Clear.html).

# Gauge in ratatui_widgets::gauge - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/gauge/struct.Gauge.html

`pub struct Gauge<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget to display a progress bar.

A `Gauge` renders a bar filled according to the value given to [ Gauge::percent](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html#method.percent) or

[. The bar width and height are defined by the](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html#method.ratio)

`Gauge::ratio`[it is](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/rect/struct.Rect.html)

`Rect`[rendered](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/widgets/widget/trait.Widget.html#tymethod.render)in.

The associated label is always centered horizontally and vertically. If not set with
[ Gauge::label](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html#method.label), the label is the percentage of the bar filled.

You might want to have a higher precision bar using [ Gauge::use_unicode](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html#method.use_unicode).

This can be useful to indicate the progression of a task, like a download.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Gauge};
Gauge::default()
    .block(Block::bordered().title("Progress"))
    .gauge_style(Style::new().white().on_black().italic())
    .percent(20);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See also

- `LineGauge`

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Sets the bar progression from a ratio (float).

`ratio` is the ratio between filled bar over empty bar (i.e. `3/4` completion is `0.75`).
This is more easily seen as a floating point percentage (e.g. 42% = `0.42`).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-1)Panics

This method panics if `ratio` is **not** between 0 and 1 inclusively.

[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-2)See also

See [ Gauge::percent](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html#method.percent) to set from a percentage.

Sets the widget style.

`style` accepts any type that is convertible to [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) (e.g.

[,](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`This will style the block (if any non-styled) and background of the widget (everything
except the bar itself). [ Block](https://docs.rs/block/struct.Block.html) style set with

[takes precedence.](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html#method.block)

`Gauge::block`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/gauge.rs.html#148-151)#### pub const fn [use_unicode](https://docs.rs#method.use_unicode)(self, unicode: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/gauge.rs.html#148-151)

#### pub const fn [use_unicode](https://docs.rs#method.use_unicode)(self, unicode: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> Self

Sets whether to use unicode characters to display the progress bar.

This enables the use of
[unicode block characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements).
This is useful to display a higher precision bar (8 extra fractional parts per cell).

# LineGauge in ratatui_widgets::gauge - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/gauge/struct.LineGauge.html

`pub struct LineGauge<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A compact widget to display a progress bar over a single thin line.

This can be useful to indicate the progression of a task, like a download.

A `LineGauge` renders a line filled with symbols defined by [ LineGauge::filled_symbol](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.filled_symbol) and

[according to the value given to](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.unfilled_symbol)

`LineGauge::unfilled_symbol`[. Unlike](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.ratio)

`LineGauge::ratio`[, only the width can be defined by the](https://docs.rs/struct.Gauge.html)

`Gauge`[rendering](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/widgets/widget/trait.Widget.html#tymethod.render)

[. The height is always 1.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/rect/struct.Rect.html)

`Rect`The associated label is always left-aligned. If not set with [ LineGauge::label](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.label), the label is
the percentage of the bar filled.

You can also set the symbols used to draw the bar with [ LineGauge::line_set](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.line_set).

To style the gauge line use [ LineGauge::filled_style](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.filled_style) and

[which let you pick a color for foreground (i.e. line) and background of the filled and unfilled part of gauge respectively.](https://docs.rs/struct.LineGauge.html#method.unfilled_style)

`LineGauge::unfilled_style`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples:

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::symbols;
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, LineGauge};
LineGauge::default()
    .block(Block::bordered().title("Progress"))
    .filled_style(Style::new().white().on_black().bold())
    .filled_symbol(symbols::line::THICK_HORIZONTAL)
    .ratio(0.4);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See also

- `Gauge`

`ratio` is the ratio between filled bar over empty bar (i.e. `3/4` completion is `0.75`).
This is more easily seen as a floating point percentage (e.g. 42% = `0.42`).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Sets the widget style.

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

# List in ratatui_widgets::list - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/list/struct.List.html

`pub struct List<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget to display several items among which one can be selected (optional)

A list is a collection of [ ListItem](https://docs.rs/struct.ListItem.html)s.

This is different from a [ Table](https://docs.rs/table/struct.Table.html) because it does not handle columns, headers or footers and
the item’s height is automatically determined. A

`List` can also be put in reverse order (i.e.
*bottom to top*) whereas a

[cannot.](https://docs.rs/table/struct.Table.html)

`Table`List items can be aligned using [ Text::alignment](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/text/struct.Text.html#method.alignment), for more details see

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ListItem.html)

`ListItem`[ List](https://docs.rs/struct.List.html) is also a

[, which means you can use it with](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/widgets/stateful_widget/trait.StatefulWidget.html)

`StatefulWidget`[to allow the user to](https://docs.rs/struct.ListState.html)

`ListState`[scroll](https://docs.rs/struct.ListState.html#method.offset)through items and

[select](https://docs.rs/struct.ListState.html#method.select)one of them.

See the list in the [Examples](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/blob/main/examples/README.md) directory for a more in depth example of the various
configuration options and for how to handle state.

[§](https://docs.rs#fluent-setters)Fluent setters

- `List::highlight_style`
- `List::highlight_symbol`
- `List::repeat_highlight_symbol`
- `List::direction`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, List, ListDirection, ListItem};
let items = ["Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3"];
let list = List::new(items)
    .block(Block::bordered().title("List"))
    .style(Style::new().white())
    .highlight_style(Style::new().italic())
    .highlight_symbol(">>")
    .repeat_highlight_symbol(true)
    .direction(ListDirection::BottomToTop);
frame.render_widget(list, area);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#stateful-example)Stateful example

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, List, ListState};
// This should be stored outside of the function in your application state.
let mut state = ListState::default();
let items = ["Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3"];
let list = List::new(items)
    .block(Block::bordered().title("List"))
    .highlight_style(Style::new().reversed())
    .highlight_symbol(">>")
    .repeat_highlight_symbol(true);
frame.render_stateful_widget(list, area, &mut state);
```
In addition to `List::new`, any iterator whose element is convertible to `ListItem` can be
collected into `List`.

```
use ratatui::widgets::List;
(0..5).map(|i| format!("Item{i}")).collect::<List>();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new list from [ ListItem](https://docs.rs/struct.ListItem.html)s

The `items` parameter accepts any value that can be converted into an iterator of
[ Into<ListItem>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html). This includes arrays of

[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`&str`[s of](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)

`Vec`[.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/text/struct.Text.html)

`Text`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

From a slice of `&str`

```
use ratatui::widgets::List;
let list = List::new(["Item 1", "Item 2"]);
```
From `Text`

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::text::Text;
use ratatui::widgets::List;
let list = List::new([
    Text::styled("Item 1", Style::new().red()),
    Text::styled("Item 2", Style::new().red()),
]);
```
You can also create an empty list using the [ Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) implementation and use the

[fluent setter.](https://docs.rs/struct.List.html#method.items)

`List::items````
use ratatui::widgets::List;
let empty_list = List::default();
let filled_list = empty_list.items(["Item 1"]);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/list.rs.html#372-375)#### pub const fn [highlight_spacing](https://docs.rs#method.highlight_spacing)(self, value: [HighlightSpacing](https://docs.rs/table/enum.HighlightSpacing.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/list.rs.html#372-375)

#### pub const fn [highlight_spacing](https://docs.rs#method.highlight_spacing)(self, value: [HighlightSpacing](https://docs.rs/table/enum.HighlightSpacing.html)) -> Self

Set when to show the highlight spacing

The highlight spacing is the spacing that is allocated for the selection symbol (if enabled) and is used to shift the list when an item is selected. This method allows you to configure when this spacing is allocated.

- `HighlightSpacing::Always`
- `HighlightSpacing::WhenSelected`- `HighlightSpacing::Always`for a better user experience.
- `HighlightSpacing::Never`

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use ratatui::widgets::{HighlightSpacing, List};
let items = ["Item 1"];
let list = List::new(items).highlight_spacing(HighlightSpacing::Always);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/list.rs.html#395-398)#### pub const fn [direction](https://docs.rs#method.direction)(self, direction: [ListDirection](https://docs.rs/enum.ListDirection.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/list.rs.html#395-398)

#### pub const fn [direction](https://docs.rs#method.direction)(self, direction: [ListDirection](https://docs.rs/enum.ListDirection.html)) -> Self

Defines the list direction (up or down)

Defines if the `List` is displayed *top to bottom* (default) or *bottom to top*.
If there is too few items to fill the screen, the list will stick to the starting edge.

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

Bottom to top

```
use ratatui::widgets::{List, ListDirection};
let items = ["Item 1"];
let list = List::new(items).direction(ListDirection::BottomToTop);
```

Sets the number of items around the currently selected item that should be kept visible

This is a fluent setter method which must be chained or used as it consumes self

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

A padding value of 1 will keep 1 item above and 1 item below visible if possible

```
use ratatui::widgets::List;

```

# RatatuiLogo in ratatui_widgets::logo - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/logo/struct.RatatuiLogo.html

`pub struct RatatuiLogo { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget that renders the Ratatui logo

The Ratatui logo takes up two lines of text and comes in two sizes: `Tiny` and `Small`. This may
be used in an application’s help or about screen to show that it is powered by Ratatui.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The [Ratatui-logo](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/blob/main/ratatui-widgets/examples/logo.rs) example demonstrates how to use the `RatatuiLogo` widget. This can be run by
cloning the Ratatui repository and then running the following command with an optional size
argument:

`cargo run --example logo [size]`[§](https://docs.rs#tiny-default-2x15-characters)Tiny (default, 2x15 characters)

```
use ratatui::widgets::RatatuiLogo;
frame.render_widget(RatatuiLogo::tiny(), frame.area());
```
Renders:

```
▛▚▗▀▖▜▘▞▚▝▛▐ ▌▌
▛▚▐▀▌▐ ▛▜ ▌▝▄▘▌
```
[§](https://docs.rs#small-2x27-characters)Small (2x27 characters)

```
use ratatui::widgets::RatatuiLogo;
frame.render_widget(RatatuiLogo::small(), frame.area());
```
Renders:

```
█▀▀▄ ▄▀▀▄▝▜▛▘▄▀▀▄▝▜▛▘█  █ █
█▀▀▄ █▀▀█ ▐▌ █▀▀█ ▐▌ ▀▄▄▀ █
```

# Paragraph in ratatui_widgets::paragraph - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/paragraph/struct.Paragraph.html

`pub struct Paragraph<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget to display some text.

It is used to display a block of text. The text can be styled and aligned. It can also be wrapped to the next line if it is too long to fit in the given area.

The text can be any type that can be converted into a [ Text](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/text/struct.Text.html). By default, the text is styled
with

[, not wrapped, and aligned to the left.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html#method.default)

`Style::default()`The text can be wrapped to the next line if it is too long to fit in the given area. The
wrapping can be configured with the [ wrap](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.wrap) method. For more complex wrapping, consider using
the

[Textwrap crate](https://crates.io/crates/textwrap).

The text can be aligned to the left, right, or center. The alignment can be configured with the
[ alignment](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.alignment) method or with the

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.left_aligned)

`left_aligned`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.right_aligned)

`right_aligned`[methods.](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.centered)

`centered`The text can be scrolled to show a specific part of the text. The scroll offset can be set with
the [ scroll](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.scroll) method.

The text can be surrounded by a [ Block](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.block) with a title and borders. The block can be configured
with the

[method.](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.block)

`block`The style of the text can be set with the [ style](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.style) method. This style will be applied to the
entire widget, including the block if one is present. Any style set on the block or text will be
added to this style. See the

[type for more information on how styles are combined.](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.style)

`Style`Note: If neither wrapping or a block is needed, consider rendering the [ Text](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/text/struct.Text.html),

[, or](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/line/struct.Line.html)

`Line`[widgets directly.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/span/struct.Span.html)

`Span`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ratatui::layout::Alignment;
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::text::{Line, Span};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Paragraph, Wrap};
let text = vec![
    Line::from(vec![
        Span::raw("First"),
        Span::styled("line", Style::new().green().italic()),
        ".".into(),
    ]),
    Line::from("Second line".red()),
    "Third line".into(),
];
Paragraph::new(text)
    .block(Block::bordered().title("Paragraph"))
    .style(Style::new().white().on_black())
    .alignment(Alignment::Center)
    .wrap(Wrap { trim: true });
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new [ Paragraph](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html) widget with the given text.

The `text` parameter can be a [ Text](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/text/struct.Text.html) or any type that can be converted into a

[. By default, the text is styled with](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/text/text/struct.Text.html)

`Text`[, not wrapped, and aligned to the left.](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html#method.default)

`Style::default()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::text::{Line, Text};
use ratatui::widgets::Paragraph;
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Hello, world!");
let paragraph = Paragraph::new(String::from("Hello, world!"));
let paragraph = Paragraph::new(Text::raw("Hello, world!"));
let paragraph = Paragraph::new(Text::styled("Hello, world!", Style::default()));
let paragraph = Paragraph::new(Line::from(vec!["Hello, ".into(), "world!".red()]));
```
Sets the style of the entire widget.

`style` accepts any type that is convertible to [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) (e.g.

[,](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`This applies to the entire widget, including the block if one is present. Any style set on the block or text will be added to this style.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use ratatui::style::{Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::widgets::Paragraph;
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Hello, world!").style(Style::new().red().on_white());
```
Set the scroll offset for the given paragraph

The scroll offset is a tuple of (y, x) offset. The y offset is the number of lines to scroll, and the x offset is the number of characters to scroll. The scroll offset is applied after the text is wrapped and aligned.

Note: the order of the tuple is (y, x) instead of (x, y), which is different from general convention across the crate.

For more information about future scrolling design and concerns, see [RFC: Design of
Scrollable Widgets](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/discussions/1924) on GitHub.

Set the text alignment for the given paragraph

The alignment is a variant of the [ Alignment](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/layout/alignment/type.Alignment.html) enum which can be one of Left, Right, or
Center. If no alignment is specified, the text in a paragraph will be left-aligned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

```
use ratatui::layout::Alignment;
use ratatui::widgets::Paragraph;
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Hello World").alignment(Alignment::Center);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/paragraph.rs.html#332-365)#### pub fn [line_count](https://docs.rs#method.line_count)(&self, width: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/paragraph.rs.html#332-365)

#### pub fn [line_count](https://docs.rs#method.line_count)(&self, width: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

**crate feature**only.

`unstable-rendered-line-info`Calculates the number of lines needed to fully render.

Given a max line width, this method calculates the number of lines that a paragraph will need in order to be fully rendered. For paragraphs that do not use wrapping, this count is simply the number of lines present in the paragraph.

This method will also account for the [ Block](https://docs.rs/block/struct.Block.html) if one is set through

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Paragraph.html#method.block)

`Self::block`Note: The design for text wrapping is not stable and might affect this API.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use ratatui::{widgets::{Paragraph, Wrap}};
let paragraph = Paragraph::new("Hello World")
    .wrap(Wrap { trim: false });
assert_eq!(paragraph.line_count(20), 1);
assert_eq!(paragraph.line_count(10), 2);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#stability)Stability

**This API is marked as unstable** and is only available when the `unstable-rendered-line-info`
crate feature is enabled. This comes with no stability guarantees, and could be changed
or removed at any time.
The tracking issue is: `https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/issues/293`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/paragraph.rs.html#388-399)#### pub fn [line_width](https://docs.rs#method.line_width)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

**crate feature **`unstable-rendered-line-info` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/paragraph.rs.html#388-399)

# Scrollbar in ratatui_widgets::scrollbar - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/scrollbar/struct.Scrollbar.html

`pub struct Scrollbar<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A widget to display a scrollbar

The following components of the scrollbar are customizable in symbol and style. Note the scrollbar is represented horizontally but it can also be set vertically (which is actually the default).

```
<--▮------->
^  ^   ^   ^
│  │   │   └ end
│  │   └──── track
│  └──────── thumb
└─────────── begin
```
[§](https://docs.rs#important)Important

You must specify the [ ScrollbarState::content_length](https://docs.rs/struct.ScrollbarState.html#method.content_length) before rendering the

`Scrollbar`, or
else the `Scrollbar` will render blank.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::layout::{Margin, Rect};
use ratatui::text::Line;
use ratatui::widgets::{
    Block, Borders, Paragraph, Scrollbar, ScrollbarOrientation, ScrollbarState, StatefulWidget,
};
let vertical_scroll = 0; // from app state
let items = vec![
    Line::from("Item 1"),
    Line::from("Item 2"),
    Line::from("Item 3"),
];
let paragraph = Paragraph::new(items.clone())
    .scroll((vertical_scroll as u16, 0))
    .block(Block::new().borders(Borders::RIGHT)); // to show a background for the scrollbar
let scrollbar = Scrollbar::new(ScrollbarOrientation::VerticalRight)
    .begin_symbol(Some("↑"))
    .end_symbol(Some("↓"));
let mut scrollbar_state = ScrollbarState::new(items.len()).position(vertical_scroll);
let area = frame.area();
// Note we render the paragraph
frame.render_widget(paragraph, area);
// and the scrollbar, those are separate widgets
frame.render_stateful_widget(
    scrollbar,
    area.inner(Margin {
        // using an inner vertical margin of 1 unit makes the scrollbar inside the block
        vertical: 1,
        horizontal: 0,
    }),
    &mut scrollbar_state,
);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Sets the style on the scrollbar thumb.

The thumb is the handle representing the progression on the scrollbar. See [ Scrollbar](https://docs.rs/struct.Scrollbar.html)
for a visual example of what this represents.

# Sparkline in ratatui_widgets::sparkline - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui-widgets/0.3.2/ratatui_widgets/sparkline/struct.Sparkline.html

`pub struct Sparkline<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Widget to render a sparkline over one or more lines.

Each bar in a `Sparkline` represents a value from the provided dataset. The height of the bar
is determined by the value in the dataset.

You can create a `Sparkline` using [ Sparkline::default](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.default).

The data is set using [ Sparkline::data](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.data). The data can be a slice of

`u64`, `Option<u64>`, or a
[. For the](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html)

`SparklineBar``Option<u64>` and [cases, a data point with a value of](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html)

`SparklineBar``None` is interpreted an as the *absence*of a value.

`Sparkline` can be styled either using [ Sparkline::style](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.style) or preferably using the methods
provided by the

[trait. The style may be set for the entire widget or for individual bars by setting individual](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/stylize/trait.Stylize.html)

`Stylize`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html#method.style)

`SparklineBar::style`The bars are rendered using a set of symbols. The default set is [ symbols::bar::NINE_LEVELS](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/symbols/bar/constant.NINE_LEVELS.html).
You can change the set using

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.bar_set)

`Sparkline::bar_set`If the data provided is a slice of `u64` or `Option<u64>`, the bars will be styled with the
style of the sparkline. If the data is a slice of [ SparklineBar](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html), the bars will be
styled with the style of the sparkline combined with the style provided in the

[if it is set, otherwise the sparkline style will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html)

`SparklineBar`Absent values and will be rendered with the style set by [ Sparkline::absent_value_style](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.absent_value_style) and
the symbol set by

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.absent_value_symbol)

`Sparkline::absent_value_symbol`[§](https://docs.rs#setter-methods)Setter methods

- `Sparkline::block`- `Block`
- `Sparkline::data`
- `Sparkline::max`
- `Sparkline::direction`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui::style::{Color, Style, Stylize};
use ratatui::symbols;
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, RenderDirection, Sparkline};
Sparkline::default()
    .block(Block::bordered().title("Sparkline"))
    .data(&[0, 2, 3, 4, 1, 4, 10])
    .max(5)
    .direction(RenderDirection::RightToLeft)
    .style(Style::default().red().on_white())
    .absent_value_style(Style::default().fg(Color::Red))
    .absent_value_symbol(symbols::shade::FULL);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`The foreground corresponds to the bars while the background is everything else.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/ratatui_widgets/sparkline.rs.html#132-135)

#### pub fn [absent_value_style](https://docs.rs#method.absent_value_style)<S: [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)>>(self, style: S) -> Self

Sets the style to use for absent values.

Absent values are values in the dataset that are `None`.

`style` accepts any type that is convertible to [ Style](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html) (e.g.

[,](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[, or your own type that implements](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ratatui_core/style/color/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into<Style>`The foreground corresponds to the bars while the background is everything else.

Sets the dataset for the sparkline.

Each item in the dataset is a bar in the sparkline. The height of the bar is determined by the value in the dataset.

The data can be a slice of `u64`, `Option<u64>`, or a [ SparklineBar](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html).  For the

`Option<u64>` and [cases, a data point with a value of](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html)

`SparklineBar``None` is
interpreted an as the *absence*of a value.

If the data provided is a slice of `u64` or `Option<u64>`, the bars will be styled with the
style of the sparkline. If the data is a slice of [ SparklineBar](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html), the bars will be
styled with the style of the sparkline combined with the style provided in the

[if it is set, otherwise the sparkline style will be used.](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html)

`SparklineBar`Absent values and will be rendered with the style set by [ Sparkline::absent_value_style](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.absent_value_style)
and the symbol set by

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html#method.absent_value_symbol)

`Sparkline::absent_value_symbol`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

Create a `Sparkline` from a slice of `u64`:

```
use ratatui::Frame;
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::widgets::Sparkline;
let sparkline = Sparkline::default().data(&[1, 2, 3]);
frame.render_widget(sparkline, area);
```
Create a `Sparkline` from a slice of `Option<u64>` such that some bars are absent:

```
let data = vec![Some(1), None, Some(3)];
let sparkline = Sparkline::default().data(data);
frame.render_widget(sparkline, area);
```
Create a [ Sparkline](https://docs.rs/struct.Sparkline.html) from a Vec of

[such that some bars are styled:](https://docs.rs/struct.SparklineBar.html)

`SparklineBar````
let data = vec![
    SparklineBar::from(1).style(Some(Style::default().fg(Color::Red))),
    SparklineBar::from(2),
    SparklineBar::from(3).style(Some(Style::default().fg(Color::Blue))),
];
let sparkline = Sparkline::default().data(data);
frame.render_widget(sparkline, area);
```
Sets the maximum value of bars.

Every bar will be scaled accordingly. If no max is given, this will be the max in the dataset.
